supports_claims: LLMs route contextual and parametric knowledge through distinct sets of attention heads, with competition occurring within knowledge types rather than across them.
Conflicting evidence persists in residual streams without erasure, while aligned multi-source signals accumulate superpositionally to determine output selection.
Entity-aware probing can mechanistically diagnose how RAG models reconcile knowledge conflicts between retrieved context and parametric memory.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper introduces an entity-aware probing framework to mechanistically trace how LLMs reconcile parametric and contextual knowledge under conflict in RAG. It provides direct evidence for how models internally handle unreliable or conflicting retrieved evidence, identifying specialized attention heads (context vs memory heads) and showing that conflicting knowledge persists rather than being suppressed. The findings are highly pertinent to a robust-RAG survey's model-evidence-use section, supporting claims about grounding, faithfulness, and knowledge conflict mechanics.
caveat: Experiments rely on synthetic counterfactual entity substitution and decoder-only LLaMA/Qwen models; generalization to naturally occurring conflicts and other architectures is untested.
notes: Code/data release pending company approval at submission time.

title: KnowGPT: Knowledge Graph based Prompting for Large Language Models
supports_claims: KG-based prompting can ground LLM responses in structured factual knowledge, complementing text-based RAG in domain QA.

Reinforcement-learning-based path extraction with reachability, context-relatedness, and conciseness rewards offers one approach to selecting informative evidence from large KGs under length and cost constraints.
Authors acknowledge that automatically constructed KGs contain noisy triples that can mislead LLMs, motivating robustness concerns for GraphRAG.
rationale: KnowGPT is a NeurIPS 2024 GraphRAG/KG-prompting framework that uses deep RL to extract concise reasoning chains from KGs and a multi-armed bandit to choose among triple/sentence/graph-description prompt templates. It is directly relevant to the modality_scenario_core section on graph/KG-based RAG in a survey on robust RAG, and its limitations section explicitly notes that noisy KG triples can mislead the LLM, which connects to unreliable-evidence concerns. Appendix or modality-case placement is appropriate because the paper focuses on effectiveness/cost rather than systematically diagnosing or defending against unreliable evidence.
caveat: Robustness to unreliable evidence is acknowledged only as a limitation; the method does not explicitly evaluate noise injection, KG errors, or knowledge conflict, so overclaiming it as a robustness contribution should be avoided.
notes: Code repository mentioned as anonymous link in paper; treat as code_only since no separate data artifact is released.

title: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards
supports_claims: Differentiable preference-based training (DPO with rollout rewards) can align data preferences across RAG modules and mitigate knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence.
End-to-end optimization of the generation module improves robustness to noisy retrieved documents and reduces overfitting compared to SFT-based RAG training (e.g., RA-DIT).
rationale: RAG-DDR proposes a DPO-based, rollout-reward training scheme that explicitly optimizes the generation and knowledge refinement agents to handle noisy documents and knowledge conflict, with dedicated Has-Answer / Miss-Answer / Internal Knowledge evaluations and a noise-injection robustness experiment. These are direct contributions to robust RAG under unreliable evidence, fitting the model_evidence_use thread on faithfulness/conflict and adjacent to evidence_construction. The ICLR 2025 publication and released code make it a solid main-text reference for the training/alignment lineage in the survey.
caveat: Improvements on knowledge refinement are limited; effectiveness is shown mainly on standard knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, not on adversarial/poisoned corpora.

title: BTR: Binary Token Representations for Efficient Retrieval Augmented Language Models
supports_claims: Efficient RAG inference techniques such as precomputed/cacheable passage representations are an orthogonal axis to robustness in retrieval-augmented language models.
Binary token representations and runtime/offline compression can reduce reader storage and latency for large passage corpora while preserving most task accuracy.
rationale: BTR introduces binary 1-bit token representations and compression techniques to accelerate the FiD-style reader and shrink storage in retrieval-augmented LMs. While it is a venue-published RAG paper at ICLR 2024 and motivates RAG via hallucination/staleness, it focuses solely on inference efficiency and does not address evidence reliability, conflicting context, faithfulness, abstention, or robustness to noisy/adversarial passages. It is at most a background reference for RAG architecture/efficiency lineage in the survey, not a main mechanistic source for unreliable-evidence robustness.
caveat: Citing it for robustness claims would overclaim; binarization could even degrade evidence fidelity, but the paper does not analyze this from a reliability perspective.
notes: Code available at https://github.com/csarron/BTR; data uses standard Wikipedia + NQ/TQA/WQ/FEVER/MMLU.

title: LaRA: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Long-Context LLMs – No Silver Bullet for LC or RAG Routing
supports_claims: LaRA provides a rigorous benchmark for comparing RAG and long-context LLMs across four task types (location, reasoning, comparison, hallucination detection) and shows no universal winner.
RAG's relative benefit depends on model strength, context length, and task type, with RAG outperforming LC for weaker models and longer contexts, and notably for hallucination detection.
LC LLMs exhibit lost-in-the-middle behavior while RAG is more robust to answer position, motivating routing strategies under unreliable evidence.
rationale: This ICML 2025 paper introduces LaRA, a 2326-case benchmark systematically comparing RAG vs long-context LLMs across novels, papers, and financial statements with four task types including hallucination detection. It directly supports the survey's evaluation chapter by providing empirical evidence on when RAG helps under long-context conditions and revealing that RAG mitigates hallucination and lost-in-the-middle issues. The benchmark addresses prior evaluation flaws (insufficient context length, data leakage, truncation, unreliable metrics), making it a useful diagnostic resource. Risk of overclaim: results are bounded by their RAG configuration (GTE-large, hybrid search, fixed chunking) and QA-style tasks.
caveat: Findings are tied to a specific RAG configuration and QA-only tasks; conclusions about RAG vs LC routing may not generalize to other retrievers, generative tasks, or noisy/adversarial corpora.
notes: Strong fit for evaluation/long-context sections; also relevant to action_control given routing motivation.

title: Provence: efficient and robust context pruning for retrieval-augmented generation
supports_claims: Context pruning via sequence labeling can dynamically remove irrelevant retrieved sentences and improve robustness to noisy evidence in RAG.
Unifying reranking and context pruning into a single cross-encoder yields near-zero-cost evidence filtering that generalizes across QA domains and context lengths.
rationale: Provence is an ICLR 2025 method that directly addresses unreliable/noisy retrieved evidence by training a DeBERTa-based extractive pruner that adaptively selects relevant sentences (from zero to all) and is jointly trained with a reranker. It is evaluated across diverse QA domains (NQ, HotpotQA, TyDiQA, PopQA, BioASQ, SyllabusQA, RGB) with needle-in-haystack and variable-length analyses, providing concrete evidence-construction insights for robust RAG. The method, model, and code are publicly released, supporting reproducibility and lineage discussion in a survey's evidence-construction section.
caveat: Scope limited to English QA with single-passage processing; gains depend on the chosen threshold and silver-label LLM quality, and the unified reranking head adds a small trade-off versus standalone rerankers.
notes: Strong candidate as a backbone reference for context pruning / noise filtering lineage alongside RECOMP, LLMLingua family, FilCo, COMPACT, and DSLR.

title: Holistic Reasoning with Long-Context LMs: A Benchmark for Database Operations on Massive Textual Data
supports_claims: RAG struggles with holistic/aggregation reasoning across many documents compared to long-context LMs
Retrieval can help weaker models on long-context tasks but full LCLM context often outperforms RAG when context grows
rationale: HoloBench is a benchmark using text-to-SQL derived queries to test holistic reasoning over long contexts, with controlled context length, information density, position, and query complexity. It includes a direct RAG vs LCLM comparison showing RAG underperforms larger LCLMs in aggregation-heavy holistic reasoning but helps smaller models, which is useful boundary evidence for a survey on robust RAG under unreliable or insufficient evidence. Best placed in appendix as supporting evaluation evidence about RAG limits in multi-document aggregation rather than core robust-RAG methodology.
caveat: Primary focus is benchmarking LCLMs rather than improving RAG robustness; RAG comparison is limited to a single dense retriever and fixed retrieval budget.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper with code and dataset publicly released.

title: ReEval: Automatic Hallucination Evaluation for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Transferable Adversarial Attacks
supports_claims: Adversarial perturbation of evidence (answer swapping and context enriching) can dynamically evaluate RAG hallucination beyond static QA benchmarks.
Even state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4 fail to faithfully use perturbed evidence, and adversarial test cases transfer across LLMs.
Faithfulness-promoting prompts do not consistently mitigate hallucinations when evidence is perturbed or enriched.
rationale: ReEval presents an automatic evaluation framework that perturbs retrieval evidence via answer swapping and context enriching to test whether RAG LLMs faithfully use provided evidence rather than relying on memorization. This directly addresses unreliable evidence robustness, knowledge conflict, and evaluation diagnostics for RAG, with human-verified naturalness of perturbations and cross-model transferability. It belongs in the evaluation section as a venue-backbone reference for dynamic, adversarial RAG evaluation under evidence perturbation.
caveat: Scope is limited to short-answer single-hop QA; perturbations modify either answer span or surrounding context but not both jointly, limiting coverage of complex unreliable-evidence scenarios.

title: Self-Retrieval: End-to-End Information Retrieval with One Large Language Model
supports_claims: Generative retrieval architectures that internalize the corpus into LLM parameters can serve as the evidence-construction backbone for RAG, with constrained decoding ensuring outputs match the indexed corpus.
Self-assessment within the same LLM can be repurposed as a relevance signal for reranking retrieved passages before generation.
rationale: The paper proposes Self-Retrieval, a single-LLM end-to-end IR system that unifies indexing, retrieval (via trie-constrained decoding), and reranking (via self-assessment), and shows downstream RAG gains on NQ/TriviaQA. It is relevant to a robust-RAG survey primarily as an evidence-construction method and as an example of model-internal relevance assessment, but it does not directly study unreliable evidence, noise, knowledge conflict, attacks, or abstention. Appendix placement is appropriate as a coverage citation for generative-retrieval-based RAG pipelines rather than a main mechanistic claim about robustness.
caveat: Does not address noisy, adversarial, or conflicting evidence; robustness claims would be an overreach since evaluation is on clean Wikipedia/MS MARCO retrieval.
notes: Code available at https://github.com/icip-cas/SelfRetrieval; NeurIPS 2024.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Lightweight NLI-based grounding verifiers can be domain-adapted via synthetic data to detect ungrounded RAG outputs at low latency
Iterative synthetic data generation with weak teacher labels and label-preserving augmentations closes most of the domain gap for grounding verification in RAG
rationale: Auto-GDA introduces an unsupervised domain adaptation framework that produces synthetic NLI training data to fine-tune lightweight grounding verification models for realistic RAG inputs, reaching LLM-level grounding verification quality at ~10% inference cost. This directly supports robust RAG under unreliable evidence by providing a practical mechanism for post-hoc faithfulness/grounding verification that can flag ungrounded generations before they reach end users. It belongs in the model evidence-use section as a method for detecting unfaithful use of retrieved evidence, with possible secondary placement in action_control since verification scores can drive abstention or correction.
caveat: The paper assumes covariate shift only and access to a representative target-domain evidence corpus; it does not directly study adversarial or poisoned evidence, so reliability claims under malicious unreliable evidence should not be overstated.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper with Amazon-science code release; evaluates on RAGTruth, LFQA-Verification, SummEdits.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
supports_claims: Graph-based RAG with structured post-retrieval reasoning can filter hard-negative retrieved clips and mitigate noise in long-video understanding.
Even when correct evidence is retrieved, LVLMs can be distracted by irrelevant retrieved clips, motivating verification and refinement steps in multimodal RAG.
rationale: Vgent proposes a graph-based retrieval-reasoning framework for long video understanding that explicitly addresses retrieval noise by introducing a structured query refinement step to filter hard negatives that mislead LVLMs. The paper documents that ~40% of failures occur even when the correct clip is retrieved, directly motivating the survey's theme of unreliable evidence and post-retrieval refinement in multimodal RAG. It fits well as a case study in the modality/scenario chapter on video RAG, illustrating how structured verification reduces context dilution from irrelevant retrieved clips.
caveat: Scope is limited to long-video QA benchmarks and does not formally evaluate adversarial or poisoned evidence, so its contribution to unreliable-evidence robustness is implicit rather than direct.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper with project page providing code.

title: EAReranker: Efficient Embedding Adequacy Assessment for Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Embedding-based reranking can assess multi-dimensional document adequacy (verifiability, coverage, completeness, structure) beyond simple relevance to filter potentially misleading evidence for RAG.
Decoupling reranking from plaintext access enables efficient context selection and may help reduce exposure of low-utility or unreliable documents to the generator.
rationale: The paper proposes EAReranker, a NeurIPS 2025 method that reranks retrieved documents by predicting an 'adequacy' score from embeddings alone, with the explicit goal of filtering documents that could mislead RAG generation. Its multi-dimensional adequacy framework (verifiability, need coverage, evidence completeness, structure) is directly relevant to evidence-quality filtering in robust RAG, supporting the evidence-construction line of the survey. Placement in the appendix/extended survey fits because the contribution is a focused reranker rather than a broad robustness or knowledge-conflict treatment.
caveat: Robustness claims are indirect: evaluation focuses on ranking and adequacy classification accuracy plus efficiency, not on adversarial/noisy evidence, knowledge conflicts, or downstream generation faithfulness.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 venue-linked; code at github.com/zjzdy/EAReranker.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
supports_claims: Reader robustness to noisy retrieval, rather than retriever quality alone, is the dominant factor governing RAG stability and scalability across retrieval depths.
Systematic evaluation metrics like RAG Stability Score (RSS) and RAG Scalability Coefficient (RSC) provide principled diagnostics of RAG behavior under realistic, non-oracle retrieval conditions.
Prompting interventions for noise filtering are inconsistent and cannot substitute for reranking or reader noise robustness, particularly in specialized domains.
rationale: RAGGED introduces a systematic framework and two new metrics (RSS, RSC) for evaluating RAG behavior across retrieval depths, retrievers, readers, and datasets under realistic (non-oracle) retrieval. It directly characterizes peak-then-decline vs. improve-then-plateau reader behaviors and shows that reader noise sensitivity is the key determinant of RAG reliability—central concerns for a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence. The evaluation methodology and findings on prompting vs. reranking are directly applicable to the survey's evaluation chapter and the discussion of model-side handling of noisy contexts.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to QA-style benchmarks (NQ, HotpotQA, BioASQ, preliminary CRAG) and does not cover adversarial or poisoned evidence; metrics emphasize aggregate stability rather than per-instance failure modes.
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); code and data at https://github.com/neulab/ragged. Strong candidate for the evaluation section and as supporting evidence for the model-evidence-use discussion of noise robustness.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: KG-based RAG can balance retrieval coverage and LLM context limits by using lightweight MLP triple scoring with directional distance encoding to produce flexible, size-adjustable subgraphs.
Truth-grounded evaluation metrics (scoreh) and refusal behavior when evidence is insufficient improve reliability and reduce hallucinations in RAG pipelines.
Retrieval size must be matched to LLM reasoning capacity since irrelevant retrieved triples can degrade smaller LLMs even while helping larger ones.
rationale: SubgraphRAG introduces an efficient triple-factorized subgraph retriever with DDE for KGQA and demonstrates how flexible subgraph size affects downstream LLM grounding, including refusal-to-answer when evidence is missing. It directly addresses unreliable-evidence concerns by measuring truth-grounded answer behavior (scoreh) and analyzing how different LLM reasoners tolerate irrelevant retrieved triples. It fits the modality/scenario section as a representative KG-RAG backbone with explicit reliability and grounding analysis.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to WebQSP/CWQ over Freebase and does not directly test adversarial poisoning or conflicting evidence; reliability claims rest on hallucination reduction via grounding rather than robustness to corrupted retrieval.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper with public code at Graph-COM/SubgraphRAG; useful as a KG-RAG scenario case with explicit truth-grounding metric and refusal behavior.

title: SePer: Measure Retrieval Utility Through The Lens Of Semantic Perplexity Reduction
supports_claims: Semantic perplexity reduction can quantify retrieval utility as belief shift in the generator, providing finer-grained signal than lexical match or NDCG-style metrics.
Evaluation of RAG should jointly consider retrieval quality and the LLM's prior knowledge, since irrelevant or already-known evidence yields zero utility.
Partial or intermediate evidence in multi-hop RAG can be diagnosed via knowledge-gain metrics rather than end-to-end accuracy alone.
rationale: The paper proposes SePer and Delta-SePer, sampling-based metrics that measure retrieval utility as the LLM's semantic belief shift toward ground-truth answers, and validates them against human judgments across simple and multi-hop QA datasets. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this provides a principled evaluation lens for diagnosing when retrieved evidence is helpful, redundant, irrelevant, or noisy, including ablations over rerankers, prompt compression, and number of retrieved items. Main:evaluation placement is appropriate because the contribution is methodological for evaluation rather than a robustness mechanism per se. Overclaim risk: the metric requires reference answers and assumes calibrated semantic clustering, so it is not directly a robustness defense.
caveat: Metric requires gold answers and Monte-Carlo sampling; does not itself defend against poisoned or adversarial evidence, only diagnoses utility.
notes: ICLR 2025 published; code at github.com/sepermetric/seper.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
supports_claims: Contextual faithfulness of LLMs degrades sharply under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual evidence, even for state-of-the-art systems.
Dedicated benchmarks with multi-paragraph noisy contexts are needed to disentangle factuality from faithfulness in RAG evaluation.
Larger model size does not reliably translate into improved faithfulness under unreliable retrieved evidence.
rationale: FaithEval is an ICLR 2025 benchmark specifically designed to test LLM faithfulness under three classes of unreliable evidence (unanswerable, inconsistent, counterfactual) that directly mirror real-world RAG retrieval failures. With 4.9K validated samples across 10 source datasets and evaluation of 18 proprietary/open models, plus analyses of CoT, decoding strategies, and sycophancy from task-specific instructions, it provides a venue-backbone evaluation reference for a robust-RAG survey. It belongs in the evaluation section as a primary benchmark for contextual faithfulness under noisy/conflicting/missing evidence.
caveat: Focused on QA-style multi-paragraph text contexts; does not cover multimodal, agentic, or adversarial poisoning attacks, and counterfactual contexts are synthetic which may bias difficulty.

title: Can Knowledge-Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation Really Retrieve What You Need?
supports_claims: KG-based RAG struggles to retrieve accurate and diverse information for complex queries that require fusing structural and textual knowledge
Process-level supervision is hard to obtain in KG retrieval; GFlowNet-style flow estimation can factorize outcome rewards to guide retrieval policies for diverse and accurate evidence
rationale: The paper proposes GraphFlow, a NeurIPS 2025 method that frames KG-based RAG retrieval as a multi-step decision process and uses a GFlowNet-inspired detailed-balance objective to jointly train a retrieval policy and a flow estimator, aiming for accurate and diverse retrieval on text-rich KGs (STaRK). For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this fits the modality/scenario chapter on graph/KG-based RAG and partially the evidence-construction angle, since it directly targets retrieval quality and diversity under complex queries. It is best placed as appendix or KG-modality discussion rather than a backbone citation, because it does not directly tackle adversarial, noisy, or conflicting evidence, only inadequate retrieval coverage.
caveat: Does not directly address adversarial/noisy evidence, knowledge conflict, or calibration; relevance is via KG-RAG scenario and retrieval diversity rather than core robustness mechanisms.

title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
supports_claims: Joint RL-based optimization of when-to-retrieve, query rewriting, and answer generation outperforms separately trained RAG modules.
Reward shaping with retrieval cost penalties enables adaptive retrieval that avoids unhelpful or unreliable database queries.
Policy networks can learn to abstain from retrieval when the knowledge base lacks relevant evidence, improving cost-quality tradeoffs.
rationale: SmartRAG unifies decision-making, query rewriting, and answer generation into a single policy network trained with PPO using environment feedback rather than proxy supervision. It directly addresses action-control aspects of robust RAG by learning when retrieval is beneficial vs. when the model or retriever cannot provide useful evidence, which is central to handling unreliable evidence. Empirical analysis on OpenBookQA/MedQA-cn/ARC-c shows the model learns to skip retrieval when the database is uninformative, a key robustness behavior. Placement under main:control is appropriate as the contribution is primarily about adaptive retrieval policy learning.
caveat: Focuses on open-domain QA with Bing search and does not explicitly study adversarial or poisoned evidence; robustness to unreliable evidence is implicit rather than measured.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper; code promised upon acceptance.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
supports_claims: Neuron-level attribution can guide scalable poisoning of RAG external knowledge, exposing a new attack surface beyond surface-level prompt manipulation.

Knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence is exploitable via targeted activation of context-sensitive neurons, with attack success exceeding 90% across multiple LLMs and QA datasets.
Existing RAG poisoning defenses must consider internal representation dynamics, not just retrieval-level filtering, to address sophisticated genetic-optimization attacks.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper introduces NeuroGenPoisoning, an attack framework that combines neuron attribution (via Integrated Gradients) with genetic optimization to craft adversarial external knowledge that overrides LLM parametric memory in RAG settings. It directly addresses the unreliable-evidence threat model central to robust RAG by demonstrating scalable poisoning under knowledge conflict, with rigorous comparison to PoisonedRAG and explicit mechanistic analysis of poison-responsive neurons. Belongs in the security/integrity section as a key attack baseline informing the survey's discussion of RAG vulnerabilities and defense requirements. Risk of overclaim is minor since results are empirical on open-source LLMs and white-box attribution access is assumed.
caveat: Requires white-box attribution access (intermediate neuron activations), limiting realistic threat scope; black-box extension is future work.
notes: Cite alongside PoisonedRAG, BadRAG, and Pandora as part of the RAG poisoning attack lineage; useful for discussing how knowledge conflict resolution at neuron level can be weaponized.

title: Training Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering through Backtracking Correction
supports_claims: Training LLMs with stepwise self-correction can improve robustness to noisy retrieved documents in RAG without requiring extensive external annotations.
Reformulating RAG as a multi-step decision-making process with backtracking enables models to better assess document relevance and avoid being misled by irrelevant evidence.
rationale: The paper proposes Backtracking Correction, a method that trains LLMs to perform stepwise assessment of retrieved documents to handle noisy or irrelevant evidence in RAG. It directly compares Label-Supervised Tuning and Chain-Supervised Tuning approaches, identifying limitations in how models distinguish relevant from irrelevant documents. This is highly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence, particularly for the model-side evidence use dimension. Published at ICLR 2025 with code available, it constitutes a useful method lineage citation for the survey.
caveat: Method evaluated only on open-domain QA datasets with relatively short documents; generalization to other RAG scenarios like long-context or multimodal is not validated.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
supports_claims: Self-synthesized rationales can train LMs to explicitly denoise noisy retrieved contexts, improving robustness to imperfect retrievers.
Explicit rationale-based denoising scales better with more retrieved documents than vanilla RAG, mitigating performance degradation under high noise ratios.
Instruction-tuning-style rationale supervision generalizes across in-domain and out-of-domain RAG tasks without extra human annotation.
rationale: InstructRAG proposes a self-synthesized rationale framework that teaches LMs to explicitly distinguish useful from noisy retrieved documents and justify answers, directly addressing the unreliable-evidence problem central to the survey. It offers both training-free ICL and supervised fine-tuning variants, with experiments showing improved robustness under increased noise ratios across five QA benchmarks. As an ICLR 2025 paper with code and strong empirical denoising results, it is a backbone reference for the model-side evidence-use perspective. Risk of overclaiming is modest since experiments focus on QA-style tasks and rely on pattern-matching evaluation supplemented by LLM-as-judge.
caveat: Evaluation is largely confined to QA benchmarks and depends on substring/LLM-judge metrics; generalization to open-ended generation or adversarial poisoning is not directly tested.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generative Question Answering for Event Argument Extraction
supports_claims: Retrieval-augmented generation can be adapted to structured prediction tasks like event argument extraction by retrieving similar QA demonstrations as prompts.
Clustering-based sampling of in-context demonstrations can improve few-shot performance for IE tasks.
rationale: This paper proposes R-GQA, a retrieval-augmented generative QA model for event argument extraction that retrieves the most similar QA pair to use as a prompt and adds an analogy loss to modulate how much to learn from it. While it uses retrieval augmentation, the focus is on improving IE accuracy in fully-supervised, domain-transfer, and few-shot settings, not on robustness to unreliable evidence, knowledge conflicts, attribution, abstention, or security. It does not study noisy/adversarial retrieval or evaluate reliability properties relevant to the survey, so it is at most a boundary application of RAG rather than evidence for robust RAG.
caveat: Citing this would risk overclaiming relevance, since the retrieval is for in-context demonstrations in an IE task, not for grounding under unreliable evidence.
notes: Code release promised at https://github.com/xinyadu/RGQA.

title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
supports_claims: Multi-agent chain communication can outperform RAG on long-context tasks when retrieval fails to surface gold evidence
RAG performance degrades when the gold answer chunk is ranked low, motivating alternatives or augmentations for unreliable retrieval
rationale: The paper proposes Chain-of-Agents as an alternative to RAG and long-context LLMs for handling long inputs, explicitly analyzing where RAG fails due to incomplete or mis-ranked retrieval. It provides useful comparison evidence for a survey section on long-context scenarios and unreliable retrieval, particularly its analysis (Figure 3) showing CoA gains are largest when RAG fails to retrieve gold answers. It is most appropriate as a case study or modality/scenario citation rather than a core robust-RAG method, since the framework replaces rather than strengthens retrieval.
caveat: Not a robust-RAG method per se; the work positions itself against RAG rather than improving retrieval reliability, so overclaiming its contribution to unreliable-evidence robustness should be avoided.
notes: Useful as scenario boundary work for long-context RAG alternatives and as empirical evidence of RAG failure modes under poor retrieval ranking.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
supports_claims: Unifying context reranking with answer generation in a single instruction-tuned LLM improves robustness to noisy retrieved contexts.
A small fraction of ranking data integrated into instruction tuning can outperform dedicated rerankers trained on much larger ranking corpora.
Reranking the top-N retrieved passages to a refined top-k mitigates the recall-vs-noise trade-off that hurts generation quality.
rationale: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM to jointly perform context ranking and answer generation, explicitly targeting the failure mode where retrievers return irrelevant or noisy passages that mislead generation. It is directly relevant to evidence construction for robust RAG, with strong empirical results across nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks plus biomedical tasks, and includes ablations showing the reranking step is essential. As a NeurIPS 2024 venue paper that establishes a method lineage for retrieve-rerank-generate pipelines, it is a natural main-text citation under evidence construction.
caveat: Focuses on single-round retrieval with text-only QA; does not address multimodal evidence, adversarial poisoning, or calibrated abstention, so should not be overclaimed as a general robustness solution.
notes: HuggingFace link in text refers to MedRAG corpus, not the RankRAG model itself.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
supports_claims: LLMs often over-rely on external context regardless of factual accuracy, motivating situated faithfulness that dynamically balances internal knowledge with external evidence.

Self-guided and rule-based confidence reasoning, especially when trained via CR-DPO, can improve robustness to incorrect retrieved contexts and generalize across QA datasets including the new RedditQA benchmark of human-written misleading posts.
rationale: The paper directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by benchmarking LLMs under knowledge conflicts with both LLM-synthesized and human-written incorrect contexts (RedditQA), and proposes SCR, RCR, and CR-DPO methods to enhance situated faithfulness. It contributes a clear taxonomy of confidence reasoning strategies, an evaluation protocol (Acc_t, Acc_f, SF), and a new dataset with verified noisy contexts, all of which are core to a survey on robust RAG. Main-text citation under model_evidence_use is appropriate because the work centers on grounding, faithfulness, and knowledge conflict resolution rather than retrieval or security per se.
caveat: Focuses on short-form QA with a single context per instance; multi-document retrieval and long-form generation conflicts are not directly evaluated.
notes: Could also be cited under action_control for CR-DPO and confidence calibration aspects; RedditQA is a useful evaluation artifact.

title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for Retrieval-augmented Generation with One Token
supports_claims: Extreme context compression via modality fusion can preserve RAG performance while reducing inference cost.
Self-distillation training can improve robustness to noisy or misleading retrieved evidence, as measured by resilience and boost rates.
rationale: xRAG compresses a retrieved document into a single token via a projector that maps dense retriever embeddings into the LLM representation space, trained with paraphrase pretraining and context-aware instruction tuning including self-distillation. It is directly relevant to robust RAG because it introduces instance-level robustness metrics (Resilience Rate, Boost Rate) and demonstrates better robustness than RAG to misleading or irrelevant retrieved documents. Suitable as a main citation under evidence construction/compression, with secondary value for evaluation and model evidence use.
caveat: Robustness gains may partly stem from underuse of compressed context (lower boost rate on multi-hop tasks), so claims about robustness should be balanced with reasoning limitations.

title: Optimizing Retrieval for RAG via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: Retrievers optimized via reinforcement learning with downstream RAG feedback can mitigate the IR-RAG relevance gap, where conventionally retrieved documents may be semantically related but unhelpful or misleading for generation.
Better traditional IR performance does not always translate to better RAG performance, motivating environment-aware retrieval optimization.
rationale: The paper proposes R3, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes embedding-based retrievers for specific RAG environments using on-policy retrieval and probability-approximated generation feedback. It explicitly identifies the gap between IR relevance and RAG-useful evidence, citing prior work on misleading and unhelpful retrievals. This is relevant to the evidence_construction perspective for a robust RAG survey, but it is primarily a retriever training method rather than a study of unreliable evidence robustness per se, so appendix placement is appropriate.
caveat: The paper focuses on improving retrieval quality through RL rather than directly addressing noisy/poisoned/conflicting evidence robustness; relevance to the survey's core unreliable-evidence theme is indirect.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 published paper; useful for the evidence construction/retriever optimization sub-area.

title: Retrieval Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
supports_claims: REALM established end-to-end training of a latent neural retriever jointly with a language model, foundational to modern RAG pipelines.
Asynchronous MIPS index refresh and salient-span masking are key engineering primitives later adopted/contested in robust RAG work.
rationale: REALM is a seminal paper introducing retrieval-augmented language model pre-training, jointly learning a dense retriever and an MLM with backpropagation through retrieval over millions of documents. It is foundational for the entire RAG line of work that the survey builds upon, but it does not itself study unreliable evidence, noise robustness, knowledge conflict, or action control. Placement in appendix:background is appropriate to credit the lineage without overclaiming relevance to robustness mechanisms. Overclaim risk arises if cited as evidence for robustness or evidence-quality handling.
caveat: Does not address unreliable evidence, attack robustness, abstention, or knowledge conflict directly; cite only as RAG foundation.
notes: Pair with DPR/RAG (Lewis et al. 2020) and ORQA when establishing the RAG foundation chapter.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
supports_claims: RAG knowledge bases and agent long-term memory can be poisoned with <0.1% malicious instances to reliably trigger adversarial actions while preserving benign utility.
Constrained trigger optimization that maps triggered queries to a unique, compact embedding region transfers across dense retrievers and resists perplexity-based and rephrasing defenses.
Backdoor and poisoning threats are especially severe for RAG-based agents in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving and healthcare.
rationale: AgentPoison is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that introduces the first backdoor attack specifically targeting RAG-based LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge base, providing a novel constrained optimization to ensure malicious demonstrations are retrieved for triggered queries. It directly illustrates how unreliable/manipulated evidence stores can compromise RAG pipelines and induce adversarial agent actions, making it core material for the survey's security/integrity discussion of unreliable evidence. The empirical evaluation across three real agents, transferability analyses, and defense study give it strong evidentiary value for main-text discussion. The main caveat is that it assumes white-box access to the embedder for trigger optimization, though transferability mitigates this.
caveat: Attack assumes white-box access to the RAG embedder for trigger optimization; defense coverage is limited to perplexity filter and rephrasing baselines.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Iterative chain-of-retrieval with learned query reformulation improves robustness when single-step retrieval fails on complex multi-hop queries.
Test-time compute can be adaptively scaled (chain length, best-of-N, tree search, learning-to-stop) to control the trade-off between answer quality and retrieval reliability.
Trained iterative retrievers remain robust across retrievers of varying quality (E5-large, E5-base, BM25), indicating partial decoupling from retriever noise.
rationale: CoRAG explicitly trains an LLM via rejection-sampled retrieval chains to decompose queries, reformulate when retrieval fails, and decide when to stop, which is directly aligned with action-control and adaptive retrieval under unreliable evidence. It also offers concrete test-time decoding strategies and a learning-to-stop mechanism that map to abstention/routing themes in the survey. Robustness experiments across different retrievers and recall improvements on multi-hop QA make it a strong venue-linked backbone reference. Overclaim risk is modest since gains are marginal on single-hop tasks like NQ, which the authors note.
caveat: Focuses on short-answer multi-hop QA and KILT tasks; does not directly evaluate adversarial or poisoned evidence, and benefits diminish on simple single-hop queries.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at microsoft/LMOps/corag.

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Mechanistic interventions on FFN activations can mitigate over-reliance on parametric memory and improve contextual faithfulness in RAG.
Benchmarks like CoFaithfulQA enable evaluation of LLM faithfulness under realistic conflicts between internal knowledge and accurate retrieved evidence.
rationale: ParamMute identifies a subset of mid-to-deep FFN layers causally implicated in unfaithful RAG generation and suppresses them, combined with preference optimization to calibrate the model toward retrieved evidence. It also introduces CoFaithfulQA, a benchmark built from six QA datasets that captures realistic context-vs-memory conflicts, and reports results on ConFiQA and FaithEval. This directly contributes to the survey's themes of faithfulness, knowledge conflict, and grounding under retrieved evidence, making it a strong main-text citation for the model evidence use perspective.
caveat: Evaluation focuses on QA settings with text contexts and a limited set of backbone models; mechanism-level claims about UA-FFNs may not generalize to all architectures or modalities.
notes: Could also be cross-referenced in evaluation section due to CoFaithfulQA benchmark contribution.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
supports_claims: Retrieval augmentation can degrade RALM performance when retrieved contexts are irrelevant, especially in multi-hop reasoning where errors cascade.
NLI-based filtering with a back-off to no-retrieval generation is an effective training-free method to mitigate harm from irrelevant evidence, but it over-discards relevant passages.
Fine-tuning with a small mixture of relevant and irrelevant retrieved contexts (as few as 1,000 examples) yields RALMs robust to noisy retrieval while preserving gains from useful evidence.
rationale: The paper provides a systematic analysis of RALM brittleness to irrelevant retrieved context across five ODQA benchmarks (including multi-hop) and proposes two complementary remedies: an NLI-based filter with back-off and a data-efficient fine-tuning recipe mixing relevant and noisy contexts. Both contributions directly target the survey's core themes of unreliable evidence robustness, model evidence use, and action control via abstention/back-off. Publication at ICLR 2024 with released code, data, and models makes it a backbone reference for the model-side handling of unreliable retrieval, suitable for the main model-use section.
caveat: Experiments are limited to ODQA with Llama-2-13B/70B and small training sets; generalization to other modalities, domains, or larger retrieval corpora is not fully established.

title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
supports_claims: KG-grounded RAG can improve faithfulness by distilling structural priors (relation paths) into LLMs via SFT plus KTO preference optimization.
Constraint-based introspection with backtracking is a viable action-control mechanism for verifying reasoning paths and triggering retries when retrieved evidence violates question constraints.
rationale: The paper proposes DP, a KG-RAG framework that combines progressive knowledge distillation for faithful relation-path generation with a reasoning-introspection module that extracts predefined constraints, verifies whether candidate reasoning paths satisfy them, and backtracks when they do not. This is directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence in the graph/KG scenario, illustrating both evidence construction (path planning/instantiation) and action control (constraint verification, feedback-driven backtracking). Case-study placement in the modality section is appropriate because it is a specific KG-RAG method rather than a general robustness mechanism, and overclaiming should be avoided since constraints are still partly hand-defined.
caveat: Constraints are predefined manually and the evaluation is limited to three KGQA benchmarks, so generalization to truly noisy or adversarial retrieval is not directly demonstrated.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 KG-RAG paper with public code; fits graph/KG modality and action-control discussion.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
supports_claims: Dense retrievers used in domain-specific RAG are universally vulnerable to corpus poisoning that appends targeted content to attacker-chosen queries, with high top-K retrieval success across corpora, retrievers, and queries.

An orthogonal augmentation property of dense retrievers explains why poisoned concatenated documents retain high similarity to queries, motivating distribution-aware (Mahalanobis-style) detection defenses that outperform L2-norm baselines.
rationale: The paper provides a large-scale empirical study (225 setups in medical Q&A plus legal Q&A) showing dense retrievers can be reliably manipulated via concatenation-based poisoning, and offers a mechanistic explanation via the orthogonal augmentation property and low query-document similarity. It then proposes a shrinkage-regularized Mahalanobis detector that achieves near-perfect detection across attacks including PoisonedRAG. These are directly aligned with the survey's security/integrity and unreliable-evidence themes, making it a main citation under the security perspective with domain-specific scenario coverage.
caveat: Focus is mainly on retrieval-stage poisoning detection; downstream LLM generation robustness and adaptive attackers against the proposed detector are not deeply evaluated.
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); no explicit code/data link found in extracted text.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
supports_claims: RAG systems can be 'pragmatically misaligned'—producing literally accurate but contextually misleading content by decontextualizing facts, omitting balance, and reinforcing query biases
Robust RAG evaluation in high-stakes domains must look beyond factual accuracy and citation grounding to assess source-intent fidelity and downstream user interpretation
Production RAG search systems exhibit query-valence sensitivity, selecting different evidence from the same sources depending on how a question is framed
rationale: This ICML 2025 position paper analyzes Google AI Overview and Perplexity on medical queries (disputed diagnoses, procedure safety/complications) and demonstrates failure modes where RAG outputs are technically accurate but pragmatically misleading—omitting controversy, decontextualizing facts, and reinforcing query biases. It is directly relevant to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence because it surfaces a class of unreliability that emerges from how models use otherwise reliable sources, and proposes new evaluation directions. Best placed as a case study illustrating the gap between accuracy metrics and faithful, action-aware communication; overclaim risk is low if framed as position/analysis rather than benchmark.
caveat: Position paper with qualitative/quantitative observational analysis on two commercial systems rather than a controlled benchmark or new method; claims should be cited as motivating evidence, not as a rigorous evaluation suite.
notes: Medical-domain case study of pragmatic misalignment in production RAG; code/data at the released GitHub repo.

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
supports_claims: Traditional RAG can retrieve semantically similar but clinically irrelevant evidence, motivating structured (KG community-level) retrieval for higher-quality context in domain-specific RAG.

Combining hierarchical KG community summarization with multi-source knowledge construction and reasoning-distilled fine-tuning improves accuracy and interpretability of healthcare predictions over naive RAG.
rationale: KARE proposes a KG community retrieval framework that explicitly addresses unreliable/sparse evidence retrieved by naive RAG in EHR-based clinical prediction, and compares against classic dense RAG baselines on MIMIC-III/IV. It is a domain-specific (biomedical) RAG paper that contributes evidence construction (multi-source KG, community summarization, dynamic relevance-scored retrieval) and reasoning-enhanced prediction, fitting an appendix discussion on healthcare/structured-knowledge RAG scenarios. It is not a core methodological contribution to general robust RAG, but serves as a useful scenario case for domain RAG coverage.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to two clinical prediction tasks on MIMIC datasets and does not directly study adversarial or noisy evidence robustness beyond naive-RAG comparison.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
supports_claims: Internal LLM signals (hidden state eigenvalues, attention kernel determinants, output token uncertainty) can detect hallucinations in single responses including in RAG settings without requiring multiple generations or external verification.
Lightweight hallucination detectors evaluated on RAGTruth can serve as efficient post-hoc reliability checks for retrieval-augmented generation outputs.
rationale: The paper proposes LLM-Check, a suite of compute-efficient hallucination detection methods using internal hidden states, attention maps, and output probabilities, evaluated across zero-resource, multi-response, and RAG settings (RAGTruth, FAVA). Its RAG-specific evaluation with white-box and black-box backbones is directly relevant to detecting unreliable generation under retrieved evidence, supporting the model_evidence_use and action_control angles. Appendix placement is appropriate because it is primarily a general hallucination detector rather than a RAG-specific reliability mechanism, with relatively modest absolute detection performance (e.g., AUROC ~55-65 on RAGTruth).
caveat: Detection AUROC on RAGTruth is modest and the method does not directly address evidence quality or retrieval issues; overclaiming RAG-specific robustness contributions should be avoided.
notes: NeurIPS 2024; codebase referenced but exact repo URL not extracted in signals.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
supports_claims: RAG datastores are vulnerable to prompt-injection-based extraction attacks that exploit instruction-following capabilities of LMs.
Position bias and ineffective context utilization are root causes of datastore leakage, and position-invariant inference combined with safety-aware prompting mitigates the attack.
Production RAG systems such as customized GPTs can leak verbatim datastore content at high rates with minimal queries.
rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper systematically studies prompt-injection-based data extraction from RIC-style RAG systems across many open-weights LMs and production GPTs, quantifying leakage rates, identifying instruction tuning and position bias as drivers, and proposing PINE plus safety-aware prompts as defenses. It is a strong fit for the security/integrity dimension of a robust RAG survey because it characterizes a concrete unreliable-evidence threat (adversarial context manipulation) and reliability/defense mechanisms. Main-cite placement under security is appropriate, with low overclaim risk since the empirical scope and threat model are explicit.
caveat: Focus is on datastore privacy leakage rather than answer correctness under noisy/poisoned evidence, so framing should not overextend it to general retrieval noise robustness.
notes: Code link referenced in abstract; PINE defense ties to position-bias literature relevant to evidence use.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
supports_claims: Context compression of retrieved documents into concise summaries can reduce distraction from irrelevant evidence while preserving task performance.
Selective augmentation, where the compressor can output an empty summary when retrieval is unhelpful, mitigates the harm of irrelevant or noisy retrieved documents.
End-task-signal-trained extractive and abstractive compressors transfer across LMs and outperform off-the-shelf summarizers as evidence filters.
rationale: RECOMP introduces extractive and abstractive compressors trained with end-task signals to summarize retrieved documents, explicitly handling cases where retrieval is irrelevant or unhelpful by emitting empty summaries (selective augmentation). This directly targets robust RAG under unreliable evidence by filtering noise and reducing distraction, supported by analyses on QA and language modeling. It is a venue-published (ICLR 2024) backbone reference for evidence construction and context compression with reliability-oriented design. Overclaim risk is modest: selective augmentation F1 versus oracle is limited and transfer to other LMs (e.g., LLaMA) is imperfect.
caveat: Selective augmentation accuracy is modest versus oracle, and abstractive compressors can still hallucinate or drop information, especially for multi-hop tasks like HotpotQA.
notes: Strong fit for evidence_construction section; also relevant secondary discussion under action_control for selective augmentation.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
supports_claims: Reliability-aware document filtering using contradiction graphs and Maximum Independent Set provides provable robustness against bounded retrieval corruption in RAG
Leveraging retriever-provided ranking or cardinal reliability signals enables a defense-in-depth approach against prompt injection and corpus poisoning attacks
Weighted sample-and-aggregate frameworks can scale robust RAG defenses to larger retrieval sets while preserving robustness guarantees
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense framework against adversarial attacks on RAG retrieval corpora using NLI-based contradiction detection and Maximum Independent Set selection that prioritizes higher-ranked documents. It provides both provable robustness guarantees and empirical evaluation against prompt injection and corpus poisoning, comparing favorably to RobustRAG, AstuteRAG, and InstructRAG on QA and long-form generation tasks. The work directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable/adversarial evidence and is a strong venue-backbone citation for the security/integrity perspective with explicit attention to retrieval reliability signals.
caveat: Defense effectiveness depends on NLI model accuracy and assumes bounded corruption; the consistent-majority assumption may not hold for ambiguous queries, and code was not released at submission time.
notes: Closely linked to RobustRAG lineage; useful for both security and evidence-construction discussion.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
supports_claims: Multimodal RAG systems suffer from attention bias toward visual tokens and knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge, requiring adaptive mechanisms to balance the two when retrieved evidence varies in reliability.
Training-free decoding interventions that adaptively reweight parametric vs contextual logits based on attention-derived reliability signals can mitigate unreliable retrieval in MLLMs.
rationale: ALFAR is a NeurIPS 2025 multimodal RAG method that directly addresses two core robust-RAG problems: knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved context, and attention bias that limits effective use of retrieved evidence. It uses retrieval similarity and query-context relevance to adaptively shift attention and fuse logits, explicitly handling the case when contextual knowledge is unreliable. This makes it a strong fit for the multimodal scenario chapter and for the model-evidence-use discussion of how MLLMs handle noisy context.
caveat: Method is decoding-only and assumes white-box access to MLLM parameters; evaluation focuses on knowledge-intensive VQA benchmarks rather than adversarial or poisoned retrieval settings.
notes: Strong fit as a multimodal RAG case for handling unreliable retrieved evidence via adaptive logits fusion.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic  Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
supports_claims: Two-stage semantic and conflict-aware filtering can defend RAG against corpus poisoning while preserving useful evidence.
Structured semantic extraction (entities, intent, relations) enables fine-grained detection of poisoned or conflicting retrieved documents.
Joint clustering plus semantic-graph filtering with conflict-aware inference reduces attack success rate across multiple LLMs and QA benchmarks.
rationale: SeCon-RAG proposes a two-stage defense (SCF + CAF) explicitly targeting corpus poisoning and prompt injection in RAG, combining clustering-based filtering, EIRE-guided semantic graph filtering, and inference-time conflict resolution across query/corpus/model knowledge. It is directly aligned with the survey's focus on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, providing both a security-integrity defense and an action-control-adjacent mechanism for resolving knowledge conflicts. The NeurIPS 2025 venue, evaluation across five LLMs and three QA datasets, and comparison with TrustRAG/AstuteRAG/InstructRAG make it a strong backbone citation for the security/defense section.
caveat: Relies on a small manually curated set of verified clean documents and multiple LLM calls, which may limit scalability and reproducibility; code availability is stated but artifact link is not clearly verified.
notes: Useful for cross-referencing with TrustRAG, AstuteRAG, RobustRAG, and InstructRAG in the defenses-against-poisoning lineage.

title: StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization
supports_claims: Restructuring scattered evidence into task-appropriate structured forms (tables, graphs, catalogues, algorithms, chunks) improves RAG over noisy long-context inputs.
A learned routing module that selects the optimal evidence structure type per task can reduce reasoning errors caused by dispersed, noisy retrieved chunks.
Hybrid evidence structurization outperforms single-format approaches (e.g., chunk-only RAG, GraphRAG) on knowledge-intensive multi-document reasoning.
rationale: StructRAG proposes inference-time hybrid information structurization for RAG, comprising a DPO-trained router that picks among five structural formats, an LLM-based structurizer, and a utilizer that decomposes questions and extracts precise knowledge. The paper directly addresses unreliable evidence problems—scattered, noisy retrievals over very long multi-document inputs (up to 200K tokens)—and shows performance gains grow as evidence becomes more dispersed (Loong sets 1-4). It belongs in the evidence-construction section of the survey since it provides a concrete mechanism for converting raw retrieval into more reliable structured context, with ablations isolating router/structurizer/utilizer contributions.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to Loong and one summarization benchmark with Qwen2 backbones; exact-match drops are acknowledged due to format loss during structurization, and robustness to adversarial or counterfactual evidence is not directly tested.
notes: Code available at https://github.com/icip-cas/StructRAG; ICLR 2025 publication.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: Multi-agent reinforcement learning can jointly optimize RAG pipeline components (query rewriter, selector, generator) with a shared answer-quality reward to address misalignment between module-level and end-to-end objectives.
Treating document selection as an RL agent within a cooperative pipeline helps filter noisy candidate documents and improves grounding in QA benchmarks.
rationale: MMOA-RAG models the RAG pipeline as a cooperative multi-agent RL problem and uses MAPPO with shared F1 reward to jointly optimize a query rewriter, document selector, and generator. This is relevant to robust RAG because the selector explicitly filters retrieved documents to mitigate noise, and joint optimization addresses the well-known mismatch where high-relevance documents do not always yield correct answers. It fits as appendix support under action/control-based pipeline optimization rather than a main mechanistic backbone for unreliable-evidence robustness.
caveat: Focuses on multi-hop/single-hop QA optimization with clean Wikipedia corpora; does not directly evaluate adversarial, poisoned, or counterfactual evidence robustness.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at github.com/chenyiqun/MMOA-RAG.

title: TRACE: Grounding Time Series in Context for Multimodal Embedding and Retrieval
supports_claims: Cross-modal retrieval can extend RAG to time-series foundation models by aligning temporal signals with textual context.
Dual-level hard negative mining improves retrieval discrimination for multimodal RAG over time-series data.
rationale: TRACE proposes a multimodal time-series retriever that grounds temporal signals in textual descriptions and uses retrieved pairs to form soft prompts for frozen time-series foundation models. It represents a scenario-specific RAG extension (time-series multimodal) and demonstrates that retrieval-augmented context improves forecasting and classification. It is appropriate as an appendix or modality-coverage citation since it broadens RAG beyond text, though it does not directly address unreliable evidence, conflict, or robustness mechanisms central to the survey.
caveat: The paper focuses on alignment quality and downstream gains, not on noise robustness, evidence sufficiency, or conflict handling, so it should not be overclaimed as a robustness contribution.
notes: Useful as a time-series multimodal RAG scenario reference; hard-negative mining could be cited as an evidence-construction technique in a non-text modality.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
supports_claims: Defining and detecting context sufficiency is a key lens for diagnosing RAG failures under unreliable evidence.
LLMs frequently hallucinate rather than abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, motivating action-control mechanisms.
Selective generation combining sufficient-context signals with model confidence improves accuracy-coverage trade-offs in RAG.
rationale: The paper introduces a formal notion of sufficient context and an LLM-based autorater to classify (query, context) pairs, then uses it to diagnose RAG failures across multiple SOTA models and benchmarks. It demonstrates that models hallucinate more than they abstain under insufficient context and proposes a selective generation method combining sufficiency and confidence signals to reduce hallucinations by 2-10%. This directly contributes both an evidence-quality diagnostic and an action-control mechanism central to a robust RAG survey, making it a backbone citation. The placement under evidence construction reflects the core sufficient-context contribution, though it could equally anchor action_control discussion.
caveat: Analysis is limited to QA datasets and does not cover summarization or multimodal RAG; autorater accuracy (93%) introduces some labeling noise in downstream claims.
notes: Bridges evidence sufficiency and selective generation; could also be cited in main:control section.

title: WebBrain: Learning to Generate Factually Correct Articles for Queries by Grounding on Large Web Corpus
supports_claims: Web-scale evidence retrieval with topic-consistency and redundancy filtering improves factual grounding in long-form RAG generation
Citation-mark-aware decoding and curriculum warm-up help attribute generated claims to retrieved evidence
rationale: WebBrain introduces a task and ReGen framework for generating Wikipedia-style factual articles grounded on retrieved web evidence, with explicit mechanisms for topic consistency, redundancy filtering, asymmetric sparsity in retrieval, and citation-mark decoding for attribution. These contributions touch evidence construction and faithful attribution under noisy web evidence, which is relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence. It is best placed in extended/appendix coverage because its main contribution is a task/dataset plus a specific pipeline rather than a general robustness mechanism. Overclaim risk: it does not directly study adversarial or knowledge-conflict robustness.
caveat: Primarily a task/dataset and pipeline paper; does not explicitly evaluate adversarial or conflicting evidence robustness, and citation-mark accuracy is only heuristically measured.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language retrieval over document page images (ColPali with late interaction) provides a simpler and more robust evidence-construction pipeline for visually rich RAG, avoiding brittle OCR/layout/captioning steps.
The ViDoRe benchmark enables evaluation of multimodal document retrieval across domains, languages, and visual element types, supporting reliability assessment of visual RAG pipelines.
rationale: ColPali (ICLR 2025) is a venue-backbone work for multimodal/visual document retrieval, directly relevant to the modality-scenario chapter of a robust RAG survey. It replaces fragile multi-stage OCR/parsing/captioning pipelines (a key source of unreliable textual evidence) with end-to-end VLM-based multi-vector retrieval and introduces ViDoRe as an evaluation benchmark. Both the method and benchmark are widely adopted reference points for visual RAG evidence construction. Overclaim risk is modest if positioned narrowly as evidence-construction for visual RAG rather than as a general robustness mechanism against adversarial or conflicting evidence.
caveat: The paper focuses on retrieval quality/latency, not explicitly on noise robustness, knowledge conflict, or abstention; cite for evidence-construction in visual RAG, not for reliability claims.
notes: Strong artifact availability (HuggingFace models, data, leaderboard); useful as canonical citation for vision-based document RAG.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
supports_claims: Test-time critique-driven refinement can correct reasoning misalignment between LLM outputs and retrieved evidence, improving faithfulness under noisy retrieval.
Training a dedicated Critic Language Model via contrastive critique synthesis mitigates self-bias and outperforms larger self-critic baselines.
Dynamic stopping mechanisms (autonomous variants) enable adaptive refinement steps without sacrificing accuracy, addressing efficiency-robustness tradeoffs in RAG.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper reframes RAG as Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning and explicitly tackles reasoning misalignment between LLM outputs and retrieved evidence via a learned Critic Language Model trained with contrastive critique synthesis, then iteratively refines outputs at test time. The work directly targets reliability under noisy/informative retrieval scenarios with empirical evaluation across seven QA benchmarks and three model families, making it strong evidence for the model-evidence-use perspective of robust RAG. It also includes an action-control element through AlignRAG-auto's dynamic stopping. The main-text placement under model evidence use is appropriate, with secondary relevance to action control.
caveat: The 'robustness to noisy retrieval' claims are mostly QA-focused and the failure analysis shows the critic can hallucinate when retrieval is incomplete, so survey should not overclaim general robustness beyond QA settings.
notes: Published at NeurIPS 2025; code released on GitHub per abstract.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained adaptive search intensity scaling enables LLMs to escalate retrieval depth and frequency when facing noisy or unreliable open-web evidence
Real-world open-web RAG benchmarks (WebPuzzle) elicit information-seeking behaviors such as conflict resolution, verification, and reflection that clean Wiki-based benchmarks under-test
rationale: The paper proposes DeepDiver, an RL framework that learns adaptive search intensity (when and how much to retrieve) for iterative RAG in noisy real-world web environments, and introduces WebPuzzle, a benchmark explicitly designed around unreliable and conflicting evidence. This directly contributes to robust RAG via action control (adaptive retrieval/abstention from over-confident answering) and to evaluation under unreliable evidence, making it suitable as a main citation in the action-control section with secondary relevance to evaluation. The overclaim risk is modest since experiments are limited to 7B models and Chinese-centric data, but the mechanism and benchmark are clearly venue-published and methodologically supportive of the survey.
caveat: Experiments are constrained to 7B backbones and a primarily Chinese open-web setting; generalization claims to English/larger models rely on translated subsets.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper; code/data not yet released at submission time per checklist.

title: Accelerating Inference of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Sparse Context Selection
supports_claims: Self-assessment via special control tokens can filter irrelevant retrieved contexts within a single model pass, improving generation quality while reducing latency.
Sparse context selection acts as an internal corrective mechanism, offering an alternative to external classifiers like CRAG for handling noisy retrieved evidence.
rationale: The paper proposes Sparse RAG, which encodes documents in parallel and uses learned control tokens to assess per-context relevance, then selectively decodes attending only to high-relevance KV caches. While the primary motivation is inference acceleration, the per-context assessment mechanism is directly relevant to filtering unreliable/noisy evidence, and the paper explicitly compares against Self-RAG and CRAG as robustness baselines. Placement in appendix is appropriate because the central contribution is efficiency rather than robustness, though the unified self-assessment design is a useful data point for evidence-filtering lineage. Overclaim risk: it should not be cited as a robustness-focused method since reliability is a byproduct rather than the explicit goal.
caveat: Efficiency is the primary contribution; robustness to unreliable evidence is a side benefit and is evaluated only on standard QA/summarization datasets without adversarial or counterfactual noise.
notes: Useful as a contrast point to CRAG and Self-RAG for unified in-model evidence assessment.

title: Chunk-Distilled Language Modeling
supports_claims: Chunk-level retrieval with trie-structured datastores offers an alternative granularity to token-level kNN-LM and document-level RAG for evidence construction.
Training-free knowledge injection via retrieved chunks can adapt model distributions including for expert/private knowledge sources.
rationale: CD-LM is a training-free chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation method that interleaves LM tokens with retrieved multi-token chunks via trie datastores, with three variants for knowledge distillation, self distillation, and expert/private knowledge injection. It contributes to the RAG methodology lineage at the level of retrieval granularity and context construction, but does not directly address unreliable evidence, noise filtering, knowledge conflict, attribution, or evidence sufficiency. Appropriate as appendix coverage for retrieval-augmented LM foundations and chunk-granularity evidence construction; main-text citation would overclaim its relevance to robust RAG under unreliable evidence.
caveat: Paper assumes datastore chunks are reliable and does not study robustness, adversarial evidence, or knowledge conflict; only tangential to the survey's core focus.
notes: ICLR 2025 published; could appear in a foundations/methods table alongside kNN-LM, REST, RETRO as a chunk-granularity RAG variant.

title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-based alignment can train retrieval-augmented LLMs to prioritize retrieved context over parametric memory in knowledge-conflict settings
Reward shaping with KL and anti-collapse penalties enables trustworthy grounding without explicit supervision on how to respond
rationale: The paper proposes Trustworthy-Alignment, a PPO-based RL method that rewards retrieval-augmented LLMs for generating responses grounded in retrieved evidence and penalizes reliance on parametric knowledge under counterfactual conflicts. It provides theoretical convergence analysis and demonstrates generalization across Natural Questions, ConflictQA-PopQA, and ConflictQA-StrategyQA, making it directly relevant to the model-evidence-use axis of robust RAG. Placement under main:model is appropriate because it represents a method lineage for resolving knowledge conflicts and improving context faithfulness.
caveat: Assumes retrieved evidence contains the correct answer; performance depends on inherent instruction-following capacity of base model and may not handle imperfect retrieval well without modification.
notes: ICML 2024 venue-published, code available on GitHub

title: LoRANN: Low-Rank Matrix Factorization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
supports_claims: Efficient approximate nearest neighbor search underpins practical RAG pipelines and vector databases.
Low-rank/quantized score computation methods can trade memory and latency for recall in retrieval backends.
rationale: LoRANN introduces a reduced-rank regression based score computation method for clustering-based ANN search and an associated library that competes with state-of-the-art graph and PQ-based methods. RAG is cited only as a motivating use case; the paper does not address evidence reliability, faithfulness, knowledge conflict, action control, or robustness evaluation that the survey targets. It is appropriate as background to ground the retrieval infrastructure layer of RAG, but not as a main citation for robustness under unreliable evidence.
caveat: Risk of overclaiming RAG relevance—paper is fundamentally an ANN/IR systems contribution with no analysis of retrieval quality's downstream effect on generation reliability.
notes: NeurIPS 2024 paper; useful only as a pointer to modern ANN retrieval backends in a background/infrastructure section.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
supports_claims: Cross-modal RAG pipelines (e.g., video-to-3D-motion) suffer from error propagation when retrieved evidence is noisy or misaligned with the target modality.
Preference-based training (DPO with dual-alignment rewards) can teach generators to discount non-informative retrieved evidence and adaptively rely on retrieval quality.
rationale: VimoRAG is a NeurIPS 2025 video-based RAG framework for 3D motion generation that explicitly identifies and tackles error propagation from low-quality retrievals via the McDPO training strategy, teaching the LLM when to use, ignore, or how much to rely on retrieved video evidence. This is directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence as a multimodal scenario case study, illustrating both retriever-side improvements (Gemini-MVR) and generator-side robustness (preference optimization with dual-alignment reward). Placement as a modality case study fits because the contribution is most informative for the multimodal RAG and noisy-evidence handling sections rather than as a core mechanistic backbone.
caveat: The work is specific to text-to-motion generation; generalization of McDPO-style robustness to text-only or other modalities is not directly validated, so overclaiming its method as a general robust-RAG technique should be avoided.
notes: Useful as a multimodal/video RAG example demonstrating retrieval-induced error propagation and a preference-training mitigation.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
supports_claims: Multi-image visual RAG requires filtering of irrelevant images to avoid distractor-induced degradation in LMM reasoning.
Vision-centric needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks reveal LMM weaknesses including positional bias and poor cross-image reasoning under unreliable visual evidence.
rationale: The paper introduces the Visual Haystacks benchmark and MIRAGE, an open-source visual-RAG framework that uses a co-trained query-aware retriever to filter visual distractors before LMM reasoning, scaling to 10k images. It diagnoses three robustness failures of LMMs under unreliable multi-image evidence: susceptibility to visual distractors, weak cross-image reasoning, and positional bias. This directly supports a survey section on multimodal/vision RAG under unreliable evidence and on retrieval-side filtering of irrelevant evidence. Placement as a case study in the modality section is appropriate since it combines benchmark and method contributions specific to vision RAG.
caveat: The benchmark is template-based on COCO objects and may inherit COCO biases; findings on distractor robustness may not generalize to open-domain multimodal RAG.
