title: DocKS-RAG: Optimizing Document-Level Relation Extraction through LLM-Enhanced Hybrid Prompt Tuning
supports_claims: RAG can be combined with knowledge graphs and hybrid prompt tuning for document-level relation extraction tasks
Threshold-based filtering of retrieved entities and sentences can reduce noise in graph-augmented LLM prompts
rationale: This paper proposes DocKS-RAG, a framework combining document-level knowledge graph construction with sentence-level semantic RAG and hybrid prompt tuning via LoRA on LLMs for the specific task of document-level relation extraction. While it uses RAG components and discusses noise filtering through thresholds, its primary focus is improving extraction performance on DocRED and Re-DocRED benchmarks, not studying RAG robustness or behavior under unreliable evidence. The contribution is task-application oriented rather than mechanistic for robust RAG, with no analysis of adversarial conditions, attack/defense, calibration, or evidence reliability that would directly support a robust RAG survey.
caveat: Including this work risks overclaiming relevance since the paper does not study reliability, attacks, calibration, or unreliable-evidence handling as core contributions; threshold tuning is merely incidental to task performance.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Lightweight proxy/multi-agent systems can adaptively control RAG actions (when to retrieve, what to query, when to stop) without modifying retriever or LLM.
Tree-structured rollouts with Monte Carlo credit assignment enable end-to-end multi-agent RL optimization of routing, query generation, and document filtering for RAG.
rationale: The paper proposes C-3PO, a proxy that orchestrates retrieval necessity routing, query generation, document filtering, and termination decisions through three cooperating agents optimized via MARL. It is relevant for the action-control and adaptive-retrieval portion of a robust RAG survey, as it combines routing, iterative retrieval, and evidence filtering. However, the paper targets general RAG alignment and accuracy rather than explicitly handling unreliable, noisy, or adversarial evidence, so appendix placement is appropriate.
caveat: Does not explicitly evaluate robustness to misleading or poisoned evidence; benefits are framed as alignment/efficiency rather than reliability under unreliable retrieval.
notes: ICML 2025 venue-linked; code available on GitHub.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
supports_claims: Visual RAG can mitigate high-resolution perception failures in MLLMs by retrieving and spatially arranging query-relevant image crops.
Adaptive retrieval that selects the number of evidence items based on model confidence and retrieval scores improves robustness across task types.
rationale: The paper proposes RAP, a training-free visual RAG framework that retrieves query-relevant image crops, preserves their spatial layout, and adaptively selects K via a confidence-guided A*-style search (RE-Search). It is directly relevant to a robust RAG survey as a multimodal case study covering evidence construction (Spatial-Awareness Layout), action control (confidence-based adaptive retrieval), and the empirical finding that too many or noisy retrieved crops degrade performance. Best placed in the multimodal/scenario section as a representative vision RAG mechanism rather than a core robustness paper.
caveat: Focus is on HR image perception accuracy rather than adversarial or unreliable-evidence robustness; the unreliable-evidence connection is indirect (noise from excess crops).
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); code at github.com/DreamMr/RAP.

title: Lift Yourself Up: Retrieval-augmented Text Generation with Self-Memory
supports_claims: Self-generated outputs can serve as higher-quality memory than fixed retrieval corpora, addressing limitations of bounded memory in RAG
Iterative generator-selector frameworks can improve retrieval-augmented text generation across translation, summarization, and dialogue tasks
rationale: The paper proposes Selfmem, a framework that iteratively uses model outputs as memory for retrieval-augmented generation, addressing the limitation that fixed corpora bound memory quality. While it represents an evidence/memory construction approach for RAG, it does not directly address unreliable evidence, knowledge conflicts, noise filtering, or robustness concerns central to the survey. It is best cited as background for evidence construction lineage in an extended appendix discussion, not as a main mechanistic reference for robustness under unreliable evidence.
caveat: The method assumes self-generated memory is reliable; it does not consider adversarial, noisy, or conflicting evidence, which is the survey's core focus.
notes: NeurIPS 2023 paper with code at https://github.com/Hannibal046/SelfMemory

title: Superposition Prompting: Improving and Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Structured prompt topologies with Bayesian path pruning can filter distracting or irrelevant retrieved documents to improve RAG accuracy under noisy context.
Parallel processing of independent document paths enables both acceleration and noise filtering for long-context RAG.
rationale: The paper proposes superposition prompting, a fork-join DAG topology that processes retrieved documents in parallel paths and prunes irrelevant paths using a Bayesian saliency score derived from P(q|d,p). While the primary motivation is inference acceleration, the path pruning mechanism directly addresses the distraction phenomenon where irrelevant retrieved context degrades RAG output quality, which is relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence. It fits as supporting evidence in the evidence construction/context filtering subarea but is not a core robustness contribution, warranting appendix-level citation.
caveat: Focus is primarily on efficiency rather than reliability; pruning is evaluated on standard QA datasets without explicit adversarial or unreliable-evidence stress tests.
notes: Code available at github.com/apple/ml-superposition-prompting

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Knowledge Graphs
supports_claims: Subgraph retrieval can filter irrelevant KG facts (87% of 1-hop neighbors are noise) to mitigate distraction in KG-grounded generation.
Graph-text contrastive learning improves consistency between retrieved evidence and generated responses, reducing hallucination in KG-RAG.
rationale: SURGE is a KG-augmented dialogue generation framework that directly addresses two unreliable-evidence problems: irrelevant retrieved facts and inconsistent generation. It contributes an end-to-end subgraph retriever, invariant/efficient graph encoding, a graph-text contrastive objective, and a new KQA metric for knowledge-verifying QA. This makes it a useful representative of graph/KG-RAG approaches to robustness for a modality-scenario section, though it is narrowly scoped to dialogue on OpendialKG and not a foundational RAG paper.
caveat: Narrow to KG-grounded dialogue on a single dataset; does not address adversarial/poisoned evidence or broader unreliable-evidence threat models.
notes: Anonymous NeurIPS 2022 submission PDF; KQA metric and graph-text contrastive learning are the most transferable contributions for the survey.

title: Fine-grained Analysis of In-context Linear Estimation: Data, Architecture, and Beyond
supports_claims: Theoretical analysis shows that query-aligned retrieved examples can amplify the effective ICL sample size by a factor of alpha^2*d+1, providing a foundation for why retrieval helps in-context learning.
Linear attention and H3 SSMs implement one-step preconditioned gradient descent on in-context examples under correlated design assumptions.
rationale: This is a theoretical paper analyzing the optimization landscape of 1-layer linear attention and H3 models for in-context linear estimation, with a stylized RAG model where in-context examples are alpha-correlated with the query. It does not address unreliable evidence, noise filtering, conflict, attribution, or robust RAG mechanisms; the RAG treatment is an idealized distributional alignment analysis. It could serve as background for why retrieval-augmented examples improve ICL sample complexity but is not core evidence for robust RAG. Overclaim risk if cited as evidence about robustness or evidence quality.
caveat: The RAG model is highly stylized (Gaussian, single shared task, no noisy/adversarial retrieval) and does not address evidence reliability or robustness.
notes: Theoretical ICL paper with a tangential RAG analysis; relevant only as background on why retrieval helps ICL.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
supports_claims: Knowledge-graph RAG combined with symbolic verification can mitigate LLM hallucinations and improve reliability in long-horizon agentic planning
Hierarchical decomposition plus retrieved structured evidence and post-hoc validators form a useful design pattern for agentic RAG under noisy or insufficient evidence
rationale: The paper introduces HVR, integrating KG-based RAG, hierarchical LLM planning, and a symbolic validator that detects and corrects infeasible plans during execution in a robotic kitchen environment. Its relevance to robust RAG under unreliable evidence is indirect but real: it exemplifies an agentic/tool scenario where retrieved structured evidence is verified by symbolic checks and corrected via back-prompting, which maps to action_control and modality_scenario_core themes. An appendix citation fits because the contribution is primarily robotic planning rather than RAG reliability mechanisms themselves, but the KG-RAG plus verifier pattern is worth noting in the agentic scenario chapter.
caveat: Focus is on robotic task planning rather than directly on noisy/conflicting retrieval; overclaiming RAG-robustness contributions should be avoided.

title: Graph-KV: Breaking Sequence via Injecting Structural Biases into Large Language Models
supports_claims: Attention-level structural biases over retrieved chunks can mitigate positional bias and improve multi-hop reasoning in RAG.
Parallel/block KV-cache encoding with shared positional encodings offers a tradeoff between efficiency and inter-chunk dependency modeling under long contexts and distractors.
rationale: Graph-KV modifies LLM attention to inject graph-structured dependencies among retrieved chunks via KV-cache prefilling and shared PE allocation, reducing positional bias and improving multi-hop and long-document RAG. This is relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence because it addresses positional bias, distractor robustness in ArXiv-QA, and context-window pressure. It is best placed as an appendix cite under evidence construction since the main contribution is attention/PE mechanics rather than a direct treatment of noise filtering, calibration, or adversarial evidence.
caveat: The method focuses on attention/PE engineering and does not directly model adversarial or unreliable evidence; robustness gains are largely incidental to positional bias mitigation.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper with public code and ArXiv-QA dataset; relevant for long-context and structured-evidence subsections.

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language RAG systems can be compromised by injecting a single optimized poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database, demonstrating a key unreliable-evidence threat in multimodal RAG.

Existing defenses such as noise addition, random cropping, and RoCLIP rematching are insufficient against optimized cross-modal poisoning attacks, motivating dedicated robustness mechanisms for VLRAG.
The retrieval stage is the primary attack surface in VLRAG: once the poison sample is retrieved, the LVLM is highly likely to generate the attacker's target response.
rationale: This ICML 2025 paper presents the first knowledge poisoning attack tailored to vision-language RAG, introducing three progressively stronger variants (baseline, single-query targeted, and class-query targeted) that manipulate VLRAG outputs via a single injected image-text pair. It directly supports the security/integrity strand of a robust RAG survey by characterizing how unreliable multimodal evidence can be inserted, retrieved, and weaponized, and it empirically shows that standard defenses (noise, crop, RoCLIP) only partially mitigate the threat. Placement in main:security is appropriate because it is a venue-backbone reference for the multimodal poisoning subarea and complements text-only attacks like PoisonedRAG, TrojanRAG, and AgentPoison.
caveat: Focus is on attack design with limited evaluation of defenses; claims about robustness implications should be framed as motivating, not solving, multimodal RAG defense.
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); first VLRAG poisoning attack — natural multimodal counterpart to PoisonedRAG for the security section.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Knowledge-graph-based indexing with Personalized PageRank enables single-step multi-hop retrieval, improving evidence integration across passages compared to standard dense retrieval.
Graph-structured evidence construction can outperform iterative retrieval (e.g., IRCoT) on multi-hop QA while being substantially cheaper and faster.
rationale: HippoRAG proposes a neurobiologically inspired RAG framework that builds an open KG from a corpus via LLM-driven OpenIE and uses Personalized PageRank for retrieval, enabling cross-passage knowledge integration in a single retrieval step. It is directly relevant to the evidence-construction axis of a robust-RAG survey as a representative graph/KG-based retrieval method with strong multi-hop QA results at NeurIPS 2024. It does not directly target unreliable evidence (noise, conflict, poisoning), so its role in the survey is primarily as evidence-construction lineage and a scenario example for graph-based RAG rather than a robustness method per se.
caveat: The paper focuses on multi-hop knowledge integration rather than unreliable-evidence robustness; overclaiming its relevance to noise/conflict/attack resilience should be avoided.
notes: Influential NeurIPS 2024 work; code and data available on GitHub.

title: RuAG: Learned-rule-augmented Generation for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Rule distillation via MCTS provides an alternative to retrieval-based context injection, sidestepping issues of document quality and context window limits in RAG.
Compressing offline data into first-order logic rules can enhance LLM reasoning when retrieved evidence is noisy or insufficient.
rationale: RuAG proposes a learned-rule-augmented generation framework that uses LLM-guided MCTS to distill data into first-order logic rules injected into prompts. It is explicitly positioned as an alternative to RAG citing RAG's dependence on retrieval quality and context window limits, but it does not directly study robustness to unreliable retrieved evidence, knowledge conflict, or attack/defense. It is suitable only as background to motivate alternatives to standard RAG pipelines in a robust-RAG survey.
caveat: Not a robust RAG method; it bypasses retrieval rather than improving evidence robustness, so overclaiming its relevance to unreliable-evidence settings should be avoided.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper with public code at microsoft/RuAG.

title: Herald: A Natural Language Annotated Lean 4 Dataset
supports_claims: RAG can be applied to formal mathematics autoformalization by retrieving related theorem instances to enhance LLM translation quality.
Domain-specific RAG pipelines can improve dataset construction for Lean 4 NL-FL pairs.
rationale: Herald uses retrieval over embedded NL-FL examples to improve LLM translation of Mathlib4 theorems into natural language, training a fine-tuned formalizer model. While the paper lists RAG as a keyword, its retrieval component is an auxiliary mechanism for dataset construction rather than a contribution to robustness, evidence reliability, faithfulness, or action control under unreliable evidence. The work is best characterized as a domain application (formal math autoformalization) without insights germane to the survey's core themes.
caveat: RAG is incidental; the paper does not study noise, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or evaluation of retrieval reliability.

title: Molecule Generation with Fragment Retrieval Augmentation
supports_claims: RAG concepts can be adapted to scientific generation tasks like fragment-based molecular design
Domain-specific retrieval augmentation can improve exploration-exploitation trade-offs in generative models
rationale: This paper applies RAG terminology to fragment-based molecule generation, retrieving hard and soft molecular fragments to guide a pre-trained SAFE-GPT model for drug discovery. While it uses the RAG framework, it does not address any of the survey's core concerns: unreliable evidence, noise robustness, knowledge conflict, faithfulness, attribution, security, calibration, abstention, or evaluation of evidence quality. The retrieved 'evidence' (molecular fragments) is from a curated vocabulary without reliability concerns, and the paper's contribution is about exploration-exploitation in chemical space, not robust evidence handling.
caveat: Citing this paper risks overclaiming RAG breadth without providing any insight into reliability or robustness mechanisms relevant to the survey.
notes: Domain-specific RAG application in molecular generation; no robustness/reliability insight.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
supports_claims: MuRAG extends retrieval-augmented generation to multimodal memory by jointly indexing images and text, enabling answers to visual information-seeking queries that text-only RAG cannot address.
Joint contrastive and generative pre-training over image-text and text-only corpora improves both retrieval and grounded generation in multimodal QA.
Error analysis reveals shortcut learning where the model relies on textual clues rather than visual grounding, highlighting a robustness/faithfulness gap in multimodal RAG.
rationale: MuRAG is a foundational EMNLP 2022 paper introducing a multimodal retrieval-augmented transformer that retrieves over image-text memory using a ViT+T5 backbone with contrastive+generative training, evaluated on WebQA and MultimodalQA. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this is a canonical backbone reference for the multimodal/vision scenario section, and its error analysis (counting, recognition errors, shortcut learning when retrieval is wrong but answer happens to be right via text shortcuts) is directly relevant to faithfulness/grounding under unreliable evidence. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as it anchors the multimodal RAG lineage. Overclaim risk is low if presented as a method/scenario foundation rather than a robustness solution.
caveat: The paper focuses on accuracy and pre-training design, not explicit defenses against noisy or adversarial evidence; robustness claims should be limited to its qualitative observations of shortcut learning.

title: Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for Outside-Knowledge Visual Question Answering
supports_claims: Entity-focused retrieval improves multimodal RAG by addressing the inadequacy and overly-general nature of retrieved knowledge in OK-VQA.
Weak supervision signals (passage contains the answer) are insufficient for question-relevant retrieval in multimodal settings, motivating stronger supervision via critical entities.
rationale: The paper proposes EnFoRe, an entity-focused dense passage retriever for OK-VQA that explicitly tackles two reliability concerns: inadequate/over-general retrieved knowledge and weak supervision based merely on answer containment. It strengthens evidence construction by identifying critical visual/textual entities and selecting positive passages that contain both the answer and the entity, making it a useful exemplar for the multimodal RAG and evidence-quality discussion. Appendix/modality placement is appropriate because the contribution is scenario-specific (OK-VQA) rather than a general robust-RAG mechanism.
caveat: Scope is limited to OK-VQA with Wikipedia/Wikidata sources; the paper does not directly study adversarial or noisy evidence, knowledge conflict, abstention, or general unreliable-evidence robustness beyond retrieval relevance.
notes: EMNLP 2022 main conference paper; code available at github.com/jialinwu17/EnFoRe.git.

title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
supports_claims: Cooperative self-play with decomposer-solver roles can improve multi-hop retrieval and reasoning quality without intermediate supervision.
Two-stage SFT plus preference-based RFT using final-answer rewards is a parameter-efficient route to stronger search-augmented LLMs.
rationale: AceSearcher trains a single LLM to alternate between a query decomposer and a context-conditioned solver, with iterative DPO that uses only final-answer rewards. This is relevant to robust RAG as an action-control mechanism that improves multi-hop retrieval recall and reduces reliance on potentially insufficient single-turn evidence, but the paper does not directly address noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence. Appendix placement is appropriate because it strengthens the survey's coverage of decomposition-based adaptive retrieval rather than core unreliable-evidence robustness claims.
caveat: Does not explicitly evaluate robustness to noisy, conflicting, or poisoned passages; gains are demonstrated on standard multi-hop QA and document reasoning benchmarks.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 published; code and models openly released.

title: TableRAG: Million-Token Table Understanding with Language Models
supports_claims: Table-structured RAG can scale to million-token tables via schema and cell retrieval rather than feeding entire tables
Query expansion plus frequency-aware cell encoding budgeting improves retrieval quality and reduces token cost in tabular RAG
rationale: TableRAG is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that proposes a dedicated RAG pipeline for large-table understanding, combining tabular query expansion, schema retrieval, and frequency-budgeted cell retrieval, with new million-token benchmarks (ArcadeQA, BirdQA). For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it is a useful modality/scenario case study showing how evidence construction must adapt to structured data and limited budgets. It does not directly study unreliable or adversarial evidence, so it fits best as a scenario case rather than a backbone citation.
caveat: Focus is on scalability and retrieval quality for clean tables; it does not directly address noisy, conflicting, or poisoned evidence robustness.
notes: Code/data link at github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/table_rag

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
supports_claims: Multimodal RAG for LVLMs requires hierarchical filtering to handle noisy internet evidence and avoid long-context degradation.
Evidence construction via website-level and content-level scoring with diversity selection improves answer accuracy on up-to-date VQA tasks.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2024 paper proposes a plug-and-play internet-augmented generation framework for LVLMs, with a two-stage hierarchical filtering model and a UDK-VQA benchmark for up-to-date visual question answering. It is relevant to a robust RAG survey as a multimodal scenario case study where retrieved web evidence is noisy and must be filtered/selected before being passed to the generator. Placement under main:modality is appropriate because it exemplifies vision-language RAG with evidence construction mechanisms; it is not a core foundational method for unreliable-evidence robustness in general text RAG.
caveat: The filtering is supervised by pseudo-scores from multi-model voting and focuses on freshness rather than adversarial or conflicting evidence, so claims about general robustness should not be overstated.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
supports_claims: RAG paradigms can be extended to graph-structured data by retrieving similar subgraphs and injecting features and task-specific outputs via message-passing prompts.
Noise-aware prompt tuning, including inner-toy-graph noise and bottom-K negative retrievals, can improve robustness of retrieval-augmented graph models to irrelevant retrieved evidence.
rationale: RAGraph constructs a key-value toy-graph vector base and uses similarity-based retrieval plus intra/inter graph propagation to inject retrieved evidence into pre-trained GNNs for node, edge, and graph tasks. It is a venue-published (NeurIPS 2024) example of extending RAG to a non-text modality (graphs) and explicitly introduces noise-based prompt tuning to mitigate noisy retrieval, which is directly relevant to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence as a modality/scenario data point. Placement in the modality section (or extended appendix) is appropriate because the robustness contribution is narrow and the evaluation is on standard graph benchmarks rather than reliability-focused diagnostics.
caveat: The robustness analysis is limited to graph-domain retrieval noise and few-shot accuracy; it does not study faithfulness, conflict, attribution, or attacker-driven unreliable evidence in the textual RAG sense.
notes: Useful as a graph-RAG representative alongside KG-RAG works; cite for modality coverage and for the inner/outer noise prompt-tuning idea.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Multimodal medical RAG can be made robust by combining domain-aware retrieval, adaptive context selection, and preference fine-tuning that targets cross-modality and over-reliance misalignment.
RAG can degrade Med-LVLM behavior by inducing copy-reference and over-reliance on retrieved text; preference data construction explicitly addressing these failure modes mitigates them.
Adaptive truncation of retrieved contexts based on similarity score gaps improves factuality over fixed-k retrieval in medical VQA and report generation.
rationale: MMed-RAG is a venue-published (ICLR 2025) multimodal RAG system that explicitly diagnoses and mitigates two reliability failure modes when evidence is unreliable: cross-modality misalignment (model ignoring the image and copying retrieved text) and over-reliance (incorrect retrieved context overriding correct internal knowledge). It contributes adaptive context selection, domain-aware retrieval, and RAG-based preference fine-tuning with theoretical analysis, all directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence in a multimodal medical scenario. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as a backbone example of multimodal/domain-specific robust RAG; it also supports evidence_construction and model_evidence_use claims.
caveat: Scope is limited to medical vision-language tasks with yes/no VQA and report generation; generalization claims to broader multimodal RAG settings should be made cautiously.
notes: Code and data at https://github.com/richard-peng-xia/MMed-RAG

title: Reference Trustable Decoding: A Training-Free Augmentation Paradigm for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Retrieval-based decoding paradigms (kNN-LM style) offer alternatives to in-context RAG by fusing retrieved reference distributions at decoding time.
Training-free augmentation via reference datastores can reduce input length overhead compared to standard RAG pipelines.
rationale: This paper proposes Reference Trustable Decoding, a kNN-LM-style approach that builds a reference datastore from training examples and fuses retrieved label distributions into the LM head output, positioned as an alternative to RAG and PEFT. It is only tangentially related to robust RAG under unreliable evidence: the 'trustable' framing concerns task adaptation rather than handling noisy or adversarial retrieved evidence, and there is no evaluation against unreliable contexts or knowledge conflicts. It is most useful as background on retrieval-based decoding paradigms that sit adjacent to RAG, suitable for an appendix mention rather than a main-text discussion.
caveat: The method does not study unreliable evidence, attacks, conflicts, or calibration; overclaiming robustness contribution should be avoided.
notes: Closer to kNN-LM lineage than RAG-robustness; could be cited alongside Khandelwal et al. as background on retrieval-augmented decoding.

title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
supports_claims: RAG can serve as an inference-time mechanism (drafter for speculative decoding) that complements long-context LLMs while showing some robustness to retrieval quality.
Integrating retrieval-augmented drafts with long-context targets can preserve generation quality even when retrieved evidence is partially unrelated, given moderate knowledge-transfer strength.
rationale: RAPID is primarily an efficiency-oriented method that uses a RAG drafter in speculative decoding to accelerate long-context inference, not a core robust-RAG contribution. However, Section 4.5 shows robustness to unrelated/low-quality retrieval contexts via a tunable knowledge-transfer parameter, which is a tangential but useful boundary data point for surveys on unreliable-evidence robustness. Best placed in an appendix as a boundary citation on RAG/long-context integration; main-text citation would overclaim its robustness focus.
caveat: The robustness analysis is limited (one stress test with unrelated context) and the central contribution is inference acceleration rather than handling noisy/adversarial evidence.
notes: ICML 2025 published; code at github.com/NUS-TRAIL/RAPID.

title: RAGViz: Diagnose and Visualize Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Attention-based visualization tools can help diagnose whether hallucinations stem from retrieved evidence or from parametric memory in RAG pipelines.
Interactive document toggling and side-by-side generation comparison enable qualitative inspection of how individual retrieved documents influence LLM outputs.
rationale: RAGViz is an EMNLP 2024 demo paper presenting a diagnostic visualization tool that surfaces token- and document-level attention scores and supports add/remove comparison of context documents, with an explicit use case of distinguishing external (retrieved-evidence) hallucinations from internal (parametric) ones. This is relevant to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence as a diagnostic/interpretability tool for model evidence use, but it is a system demo rather than a methodological or evaluation contribution, so appendix-level citation is appropriate. The scenario tag of vision_multimodal appears to be a keyword false positive; the system targets text RAG. Risk of overclaim: attention is only a heuristic for influence, as the authors themselves note.
caveat: Demo paper that equates attention magnitude with document influence; no quantitative evaluation of diagnostic accuracy or robustness benefit.
notes: Not actually multimodal despite collection tag; useful as diagnostic-tool reference for evidence-use analysis.

title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained vision-language agents with visual perception actions (crop, zoom) can iteratively refine retrieved evidence in multimodal RAG to better handle visually rich, noisy documents.
Integrating retrieval-quality rewards (NDCG-based) with model-based outcome rewards improves both retrieval precision and answer faithfulness in agentic multimodal RAG.
rationale: VRAG-RL is a NeurIPS 2025 paper that introduces an RL framework for visual RAG with a dedicated action space (search, region-select, crop, zoom) and a composite reward that explicitly penalizes retrieving irrelevant images. It directly addresses unreliable visual evidence by training the VLM to issue better queries and perceptually focus on information-dense regions, reducing noise in long visual contexts. It belongs in the modality chapter as a backbone vision RAG method and also supports the action-control narrative through RL-driven adaptive retrieval and perception.
caveat: Robustness claims are demonstrated on three visual document QA benchmarks rather than adversarial or poisoned-evidence settings, so its contribution to unreliable-evidence robustness is indirect (noise via retrieval failure rather than malicious or conflicting evidence).
notes: Code at Alibaba-NLP/VRAG; relevant baselines include Search-R1, ColPali, ViDoSeek.

title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
supports_claims: Memory-augmented and amortization-based adaptation can complement RAG by aggregating compressed document representations to mitigate single-document retrieval errors.
Joint use of MAC with retrievers like BM25, Contriever, and DPR improves QA accuracy over retrieval alone, suggesting context aggregation as a path to more robust evidence use.
rationale: MAC proposes amortizing documents into PEFT modulations stored in a memory bank, aggregated per query to adapt a frozen LM, and shows it can combine with BM25/Contriever/DPR to improve QA. It is tangential to robust RAG under unreliable evidence but offers a complementary memory-augmented alternative to retrieval and discusses sensitivity of RAG to counterfactual or misconfigured retrieved evidence. Appendix placement is appropriate as background/alternative method rather than a main mechanistic contribution to evidence robustness. Overclaim risk: paper does not directly study noise, conflict, or attacks on retrieved evidence.
caveat: Does not directly evaluate robustness to noisy, counterfactual, or adversarial retrieved evidence; framed as online adaptation rather than reliability of RAG.
notes: Useful as a memory-augmented alternative/complement to RAG in the related-work or appendix section.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language models with late interaction enable end-to-end visual document retrieval that bypasses brittle OCR/layout pipelines for multimodal RAG.
The ViDoRe benchmark provides page-level retrieval evaluation across modalities, domains, and languages for visually rich documents.
Late-interaction multi-vector embeddings over image patches outperform text-only and contrastive VLM bi-encoders on visually rich document retrieval.
rationale: ColPali introduces a PaliGemma-based late-interaction retriever that embeds document page images directly and largely outperforms OCR/captioning pipelines and contrastive VLM bi-encoders on the new ViDoRe benchmark. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this is a canonical backbone for visual/multimodal evidence construction and a reference benchmark for retrieval evaluation in long, visually rich documents. The paper also touches on interpretability via similarity maps and points to abstention/confidence as future work, making it suitable for the multimodal/scenario chapter.
caveat: Primary focus is retrieval performance and efficiency, not robustness to unreliable or adversarial evidence; reliability/abstention is only mentioned as future work.
notes: ICLR 2025 published; resources released under open licenses on HuggingFace.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
supports_claims: Multimodal RAG for LVLMs requires hierarchical filtering of noisy web search results to surface helpful evidence
Diversity-aware selection of retrieved segments mitigates bias from redundant or repetitive contexts in internet-augmented generation
Up-to-date knowledge VQA benchmarks (UDK-VQA) enable evaluating LVLMs' reliance on retrieved evidence beyond training-time knowledge
rationale: The paper proposes a plug-and-play internet-augmented RAG framework for LVLMs with a hierarchical website+content filter and diversity selection, directly addressing unreliable/noisy web evidence in a multimodal scenario. It also contributes UDK-VQA, an evaluation benchmark for up-to-date knowledge VQA, useful as a case study for multimodal RAG and evidence construction under noisy retrieval. Placement under main:modality is appropriate since the framework illustrates filtering and diversity mechanisms specific to vision-language RAG with web search. Overclaim risk: filtering is supervised by pseudo-labels from multi-model voting rather than principled uncertainty/abstention, so it should not be cited as a general robustness or calibration solution.
caveat: Pseudo-label supervision and dataset-specific filtering limit generality; no formal treatment of calibration, abstention, or adversarial/poisoned evidence.
notes: NeurIPS 2024 venue-linked; project page exists but full code/data release status unclear from text.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Graph foundation models with query-dependent GNNs can mitigate noise and incompleteness in KG-indexed retrieval for RAG, enabling single-step multi-hop reasoning.
Pre-training a transferable GFM retriever on large-scale KGs yields generalization to unseen domain-specific RAG corpora without fine-tuning.
rationale: GFM-RAG proposes a graph foundation model retriever that explicitly targets noise and incompleteness in KG-based evidence structures, a core form of unreliable evidence in GraphRAG. It is a venue-linked (NeurIPS 2025) contribution that advances evidence construction for graph/KG scenario RAG, with strong empirical comparisons across multi-hop QA and domain-specific datasets. Placement in the modality/scenario section is appropriate as a backbone reference for graph_kg RAG, though it does not directly address adversarial poisoning or calibration/abstention.
caveat: The paper frames robustness narrowly as handling graph noise/incompleteness via GNN reasoning; it does not study adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflicts, or abstention under unreliable evidence.
notes: Project page https://rmanluo.github.io/gfm-rag indicates code/data availability.

title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
supports_claims: Graph-structured RAG can mitigate hallucination by retrieving connected subgraphs rather than treating triples in isolation.
Formulating subgraph retrieval as a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree problem enables scalable, context-preserving evidence construction over textual graphs.
Combining GNN soft prompts with textualized retrieved subgraphs improves grounding and reduces invalid node/edge citations in graph QA.
rationale: G-Retriever introduces the first general retrieval-augmented generation framework for textual graphs, formulating subgraph retrieval as a PCST optimization to keep retrieved evidence connected, relevant, and bounded in size. The paper directly tackles hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved subgraphs and quantifies reductions in invalid nodes/edges, which is core evidence for a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence in the graph/KG scenario. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because it is a canonical NeurIPS-published graph RAG backbone with released code and datasets.
caveat: Retrieval is static and non-trainable, and hallucination evaluation is on a small manual sample (100 responses), so claims about robustness should not be overstated.
notes: GraphQA benchmark and PCST retrieval are reusable artifacts for graph RAG evaluation.

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
supports_claims: KG community-level retrieval can address sparse and semantically misleading retrieval in traditional RAG for high-stakes domains like clinical prediction.
Combining structured KG retrieval with multitask fine-tuning enables interpretable reasoning chains alongside predictions in domain-specific RAG.
Multi-source KG construction (biomedical KG, corpus, LLM-derived triples) improves contextual relevance compared to naive dense retrieval.
rationale: KARE integrates hierarchical KG community detection with LLM reasoning for EHR-based mortality and readmission prediction, explicitly framing the work as addressing the limitations of traditional RAG that retrieves semantically similar but clinically irrelevant information. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it serves as a representative case study of graph/KG-based evidence construction in a biomedical scenario, with concrete ablations isolating retrieval components (node hits, coherence, theme relevance). Placement in the modality/scenario section is appropriate because the contribution is scenario-specific rather than a general robustness mechanism. Overclaim risk: gains are largely from domain knowledge structuring, not directly from adversarial or noisy-evidence robustness.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to MIMIC datasets and two clinical prediction tasks, and the framework does not directly address adversarial or poisoned evidence.

title: Multi-Hop Paragraph Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
supports_claims: Iterative multi-hop retrieval with question reformulation can improve evidence coverage for open-domain QA over single-step TF-IDF retrieval.
Sentence-level paragraph encodings enable finer-grained relevance scoring than single paragraph vectors, useful when only part of a paragraph is relevant.
rationale: MUPPET proposes an iterative paragraph retriever with reformulated question encodings and sentence-level representations, evaluated on SQuAD-Open and HotpotQA. It is foundational retrieval work for multi-hop open-domain QA but predates RAG terminology and does not address unreliable evidence, faithfulness, calibration, or attacks. It is relevant only as background for multi-step retrieval foundations and could be cited in an appendix on retrieval/evidence-construction lineage.
caveat: Paper focuses on retrieval accuracy and end-task EM/F1; it does not analyze noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence and offers no robustness mechanism beyond search-space restriction.
notes: ACL 2019 venue-linked; MUPPET code on GitHub.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Graph/KG-augmented RAG with Personalized PageRank and LLM-based triple filtering improves retrieval robustness across factual, multi-hop, and discourse tasks compared with embedding-only RAG.
Recognition-memory style triple filtering and dense-sparse integration are effective mechanisms for reducing noise from LLM-generated KG structures in RAG pipelines.
rationale: HippoRAG 2 is an ICML 2025 graph/KG-augmented RAG method that combines OpenIE-extracted KGs, Personalized PageRank, dense-sparse integration of passages and phrases, and an LLM-based triple filter (recognition memory) to retrieve more reliable evidence across simple, multi-hop, and long-discourse QA. It is directly relevant to a robust RAG survey as a backbone graph-based retrieval method and as an example of evidence filtering to mitigate noisy KG triples. Main:modality is appropriate because the paper's central contribution is in the graph/KG RAG scenario, while also providing useful evidence-construction insights.
caveat: The paper does not explicitly target adversarial or unreliable-evidence robustness (e.g., poisoning, conflicts); claims about robustness are largely about cross-task consistency and corpus expansion.
notes: Code/data at github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG; useful as a representative KG-RAG method in the modality/scenario section.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
supports_claims: Heuristic multimodal RAG with fixed retrieval pipelines produces non-adaptive and overloaded queries that fail on dynamic, multi-hop, or cross-modal evidence needs.
Self-adaptive planning agents that decompose multimodal questions into sub-question chains with tool-selective retrieval improve robustness to unreliable or insufficient evidence.
Dyn-VQA provides a benchmark that stresses mRAG along rapidly changing answers, multimodal knowledge needs, and multi-hop reasoning.
rationale: The paper proposes Dyn-VQA, an ICLR 2025 benchmark explicitly designed to expose rigidity failures of heuristic multimodal RAG, and OmniSearch, a self-adaptive planning agent that dynamically chooses retrieval actions and tools based on intermediate evidence. It directly supports a robust-RAG survey on multimodal evidence construction and adaptive retrieval control, with quantitative comparisons against heuristic mRAG, generative search engines, and human baselines. Both dataset and code are open-sourced, strengthening reproducibility as a venue backbone for the multimodal/scenario chapter.
caveat: Evaluation relies on F1-Recall token overlap, which can over- or underestimate factuality; the agent loop can also over-retrieve or get stuck on grounding failures, limiting strong claims about full robustness.
notes: Strong fit for main:modality; also relevant to action_control and evaluation subsections.

title: Think-on-Graph 2.0: Deep and Faithful Large Language Model Reasoning with Knowledge-guided Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Tight-coupling hybrid retrieval that combines knowledge graphs with text documents can mitigate the incompleteness of KGs and the shallow semantic matching of text-only RAG for multi-hop reasoning.
Iterative knowledge-guided retrieval with entity pruning and context reranking improves faithfulness and reduces hallucination compared to loose-coupling hybrid RAG approaches.
rationale: ToG-2 proposes a KG-guided iterative hybrid RAG framework that alternates graph search and context retrieval, using each modality to refine the other for deeper and more faithful reasoning. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it is a representative graph/KG scenario backbone that addresses incomplete/insufficient evidence by combining structured and unstructured sources and includes iterative sufficiency checks. Best placed as a case study in the modality/scenario chapter since its robustness claims are tied to KG structure rather than general unreliable-evidence defenses.
caveat: The paper does not directly address adversarial or noisy/poisoned evidence; its faithfulness claims rest on retrieval depth, not robustness to deliberately unreliable contexts.
notes: ICLR 2025; code at github.com/IDEA-FinAI/ToG-2

title: Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
supports_claims: Multilingual knowledge graphs can serve as structured evidence sources for retrieval-augmented generation in cross-cultural machine translation, addressing entity-name translation challenges.
Explicit (text-level) and implicit (embedding-level) knowledge integration are complementary fusion strategies for incorporating retrieved KG entities into encoder-decoder generators.
Even with gold retrieved evidence, generators may fail to fully exploit it, indicating that knowledge integration—not retrieval alone—can be the bottleneck for RAG reliability.
rationale: The paper proposes KG-MT, a RAG pipeline that retrieves entities from a multilingual KG (Wikidata) via a contrastively-trained dense retriever with hard-negative mining, and integrates them through explicit text concatenation and implicit embedding fusion into MT encoder-decoders. It also introduces XC-Translate, a manually curated benchmark, and provides an ablation showing only modest gains from gold knowledge over retrieved knowledge, highlighting the generator's limited ability to exploit evidence—directly relevant to robust evidence use. It fits the graph_kg modality discussion of the survey but is application-specific (MT), so appendix-level citation is appropriate.
caveat: Scope is narrow to cross-cultural MT and entity-name translation; the robustness analysis (gold vs retrieved) is limited and not framed as a general unreliable-evidence study.
notes: EMNLP 2024 main; code and dataset at https://github.com/apple/ml-kg-mt.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
supports_claims: Retrieval-augmented generation can be extended to graph learning by constructing a toy-graph vector library and injecting retrieved subgraph features and labels through message-passing prompts.
Noise-aware prompt tuning with deliberately retrieved irrelevant or bottom-K subgraphs improves robustness against noisy retrieval in graph RAG.
Inverse importance sampling helps surface long-tail knowledge in the graph retrieval base, mitigating bias toward high-degree nodes.
rationale: RAGraph extends RAG to GNNs by building a key-value toy-graph base and using intra/inter graph propagation to integrate retrieved hidden embeddings and task-specific outputs, evaluated across node, edge, and graph tasks. Crucially for a robust-RAG survey, it includes explicit noise-handling mechanisms (inner-toy-graph noise and bottom-K toy-graph noise during training) and an inverse importance sampling strategy to mitigate long-tail bias, both directly relevant to unreliable-evidence robustness. The graph_kg scenario coverage and NeurIPS 2024 venue make it a strong main-text citation in the modality/scenario section. Overclaim risk is moderate: robustness evaluation is performance-centric and lacks dedicated adversarial or knowledge-conflict benchmarks.
caveat: Noise robustness is demonstrated via accuracy on standard benchmarks rather than dedicated unreliable-evidence stress tests, and the approach is specific to graph-structured retrieval rather than general RAG.
notes: NeurIPS 2024 paper with code at github.com/Artessay/RAGraph; relevant for graph-RAG section of modality scenarios.

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering
supports_claims: Late interaction retrievers (ColBERT-style) improve fine-grained question-table matching over single-vector DPR for open-domain TableQA.
Binary relevance tokens prepended to generated answers act as a self-assessed reliability signal that filters unreliable retrieved tables at inference.
rationale: LI-RAGE combines late-interaction table retrieval, joint retriever-reader training with explicit table-level signals (RAGE loss), and a binary relevance prefix that lets the reader flag whether a retrieved table is a reliable answer source. The relevance-token mechanism is directly pertinent to robust RAG since it provides a learned signal to discount non-gold tables that otherwise mislead generation. The paper is best placed in a table/structured-RAG section of the survey, with secondary mention in action_control discussion of reliability filtering. It is a narrow TableQA contribution rather than a general robustness study, so main-text emphasis should be limited.
caveat: Tested only on two TableQA benchmarks (one quite small) with look-up questions; the reliability-token idea is not evaluated against adversarial or noisy-evidence settings, so robustness claims should not be overstated.
notes: ACL 2023 short paper; code at github.com/amazon-science/robust-tableqa.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
supports_claims: Reader robustness to retrieval noise, not retriever quality, is the primary determinant of RAG stability and scalability across configurations.

Systematic evaluation across retrieval depths reveals two distinct reader behaviors (improve-then-plateau vs peak-then-decline), motivating stability/scalability metrics (RSS, RSC) for diagnosing RAG reliability.
Prompt-based relevance instructions provide inconsistent noise mitigation and cannot substitute for reader-level noise robustness.
rationale: RAGGED introduces a systematic evaluation framework with two new diagnostic metrics (RSS, RSC) for assessing RAG performance under realistic noisy retrieval across multiple retrievers, readers, and datasets (NQ, HotpotQA, BioASQ). It directly addresses unreliable-evidence robustness by showing that reader noise sensitivity—rather than retriever quality—drives downstream stability, and that retrieval-side fixes like reranking or prompting are insufficient. As an ICML 2025 paper with released code/data, it fits naturally as a backbone citation in the evaluation section of a robust-RAG survey.
caveat: Scope is limited to text QA with F1-based metrics and uses naturally retrieved noise rather than adversarial/poisoned evidence, so claims about full unreliable-evidence robustness should not be overstated.
notes: Scenario metadata says table_structured but the paper does not focus on tables; it spans open-domain and biomedical QA.

title: Retrieval Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
supports_claims: REALM established end-to-end learned retrieval jointly trained with a masked language model, a foundational paradigm for retrieval-augmented generation.
Pre-training a dense retriever with MIPS-based document selection over Wikipedia is a precursor to modern RAG pipelines whose reliability under noisy evidence is later studied.
rationale: REALM is a seminal work that introduced jointly pre-training a neural knowledge retriever with a masked language model and backpropagating through a MIPS retrieval step over a Wikipedia-scale corpus. While it does not directly address robustness to unreliable evidence, knowledge conflict, or attacks, it is a foundational reference for the RAG lineage that the survey builds upon, including ideas like null-document handling and salient-span masking that hint at evidence sufficiency. Citing it as background is appropriate; overclaiming its contribution to robustness should be avoided.
caveat: REALM focuses on clean Wikipedia retrieval and Open-QA accuracy, not on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, abstention, or evaluation diagnostics central to the survey.
notes: Classic foundational RAG paper; suitable as a background/foundation reference rather than main mechanistic evidence.

title: Retrieval augmented text-to-SQL generation for epidemiological question answering using electronic health records
supports_claims: RAG with in-domain demonstration retrieval improves text-to-SQL accuracy on small, specialized biomedical EHR datasets compared to static prompting.
Domain-specific RAG applications in structured/tabular healthcare data benefit from medical entity normalization integrated into the retrieval pipeline.
rationale: The paper applies RAG to text-to-SQL over EHR/claims databases following OMOP-CDM, integrating a medical coding step and benchmarking several LLMs with simple/advanced prompts and top-k retrieval. It is a domain application that demonstrates RAG gains in a structured-data biomedical scenario, but does not directly study unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, or robustness mechanisms. It is best cited as a boundary example covering structured/biomedical RAG scenarios in an appendix, with no overclaim about reliability contributions.
caveat: Limited dataset size, narrow epidemiological scope, and no direct treatment of unreliable evidence, attacks, or calibration; gains are mostly few-shot demonstration effects.
notes: ACL Anthology venue paper with public dataset and code at the Bayer-Group GitHub.

title: TableRAG: Million-Token Table Understanding with Language Models
supports_claims: Schema-plus-cell retrieval with query expansion enables scalable table-grounded RAG over million-token tables, mitigating context-length and lost-in-the-middle issues.
Frequency-aware cell encoding and budgeted retrieval provide a tractable evidence-construction strategy for large structured tables.
Dedicated table RAG benchmarks (ArcadeQA, BirdQA, synthetic TabFact) expose scalability and retrieval-quality gaps in prior table prompting methods.
rationale: TableRAG is a venue-backbone NeurIPS 2024 paper that adapts RAG to large-scale table understanding via schema and cell retrieval with query expansion and an encoding budget. It is directly relevant to the survey's modality/scenario chapter on table-structured RAG and supports evidence-construction discussions about retrieval precision/recall and prompt compression under unreliable or oversized evidence. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because it is one of the canonical large-table RAG frameworks and introduces useful benchmarks for evaluation.
caveat: Focuses on QA accuracy and retrieval F1 rather than on adversarial or noisy-evidence robustness; claims about unreliable-evidence handling should not be overstated.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
supports_claims: Joint training of dense retriever and generator in multimodal OK-VQA can outperform two-step pipelines and standard RAG when pseudo-relevance labels are noisy.
Diagnostic metrics (HSR/FSR) and analysis show how unreliable pseudo-relevance signals can mislead retriever training and how combining model predictions with relevance labels mitigates this.
rationale: This EMNLP 2022 paper introduces RA-VQA, a joint retrieval-generation framework for OK-VQA with vision-to-language transformation and a loss that combines pseudo-relevance with model predictions to avoid misleading document scoring. It directly engages with unreliable evidence concerns by showing how standard RAG loss can upvote irrelevant documents and proposes diagnostic metrics (HSR/FSR, PRRecall) to analyze retrieval-generation interaction. As a venue-backbone multimodal RAG paper, it fits the modality/scenario chapter and also provides secondary evidence-use insights relevant to the survey.
caveat: Scope is limited to OK-VQA/FVQA with Google Search/KG corpora; the 'unreliable evidence' framing is implicit through pseudo-relevance analysis rather than adversarial or corrupted retrieval settings.
notes: Code repo URL appears truncated in extraction; full repo is github.com/LinWeizheDragon/Retrieval-Augmented-Visual-Question-Answering.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic  Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
supports_claims: Two-stage semantic filtering combining cluster-based and entity-intent-relation graph reasoning can defend RAG against corpus poisoning while preserving useful evidence.
Conflict-aware filtering that cross-checks retrieved documents against query intent, other retrieved evidence, and the model's internal knowledge mitigates knowledge conflicts in RAG generation.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes SeCon-RAG, a two-stage defense that combines semantic/clustering filtering with conflict-aware filtering using an Entity-Intent-Relation Extractor to handle corpus poisoning and prompt injection. It directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by tackling both adversarial contamination and internal/external knowledge conflicts, with experiments across five LLMs and three QA datasets against PoisonedRAG and PIA. It is a strong main-text citation for the security/integrity strand and also informs evidence construction and conflict resolution discussions.
caveat: Evaluated only on open-domain QA datasets and relies on LLM-based semantic extraction plus a small manually verified clean reference set, which adds runtime overhead and may not generalize to multimodal or domain-specific RAG.
notes: Scenario tag in metadata (table_structured) does not match the paper, which targets general open-domain QA defense.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Subgraph-based KG retrieval with flexible size and structural encoding improves evidence coverage and reduces hallucinations in KG-RAG.
Adjustable retrieval size matters: more triples help capable LLMs but degrade smaller LLMs, reflecting the model-evidence capacity tradeoff.
Knowledge-grounded prompting over retrieved subgraphs improves truth-grounded QA and supports abstention when evidence is insufficient.
rationale: SubgraphRAG is an ICLR 2025 KG-based RAG framework that uses a lightweight MLP with parallel triple scoring and Directional Distance Encoding to retrieve flexible-size subgraphs, then prompts unfine-tuned LLMs to reason over them. It directly contributes to the graph/KG scenario in robust RAG, addressing evidence sufficiency, irrelevant-context degradation, hallucination reduction, and explicit refusal behavior when evidence is missing. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as it is a representative venue-backbone for KG-RAG and also offers insights on evidence-size tradeoffs and grounding. Overclaim risk is modest since results focus on WebQSP/CWQ KGQA benchmarks.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to two Freebase-based KGQA benchmarks; robustness to noisy or adversarial KG evidence is not directly tested.

title: RAGLAB: A Modular and Research-Oriented Unified Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Unified frameworks like RAGLAB enable fair comparison of RAG algorithms by aligning generators, retrievers, instructions, and seeds across benchmarks.

Reproducing 6 representative RAG algorithms across 10 benchmarks reveals that adaptive/self-reflective methods (e.g., Self-RAG) benefit substantially from stronger base models, while naive RAG can underperform direct LLMs on multiple-choice tasks.
rationale: RAGLAB is a modular, open-source toolkit that reproduces six RAG algorithms and standardizes generators, retrievers, instructions, and metrics for fair comparison across ten benchmarks. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it is most useful as evaluation infrastructure and as a reference for comparative methodology rather than as a direct contribution on noisy-evidence robustness. Appendix placement is appropriate because it supports breadth on evaluation frameworks without being a core mechanistic reference. Overclaim risk: it does not specifically test unreliable/adversarial evidence conditions.
caveat: Framework/demo paper; does not directly address noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence robustness or calibration.
notes: EMNLP 2024 System Demonstrations; code at github.com/fate-ubw/RAGLab.

title: ReMindRAG: Low-Cost LLM-Guided Knowledge Graph Traversal for Efficient RAG
supports_claims: LLM-guided knowledge graph traversal with node exploration and exploitation can balance retrieval effectiveness and cost efficiency in KG-RAG systems.
Memorizing traversal experience within KG edge embeddings enables train-free reuse across similar queries and supports self-correction over repeated retrievals.
rationale: ReMindRAG proposes an LLM-guided KG traversal method with a train-free memory replay mechanism stored in edge embeddings, evaluated on LooGLE and HotpotQA with multiple LLM backbones. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it is relevant mainly as a KG-RAG modality contribution and as an example of iterative self-correction through retrieved-path memory, but its primary framing is efficiency rather than handling unreliable or adversarial evidence. Appendix placement in the modality/scenario coverage section is appropriate; overclaiming robustness from its self-correction analysis should be avoided.
caveat: The paper centers on cost-efficiency and traversal accuracy rather than explicit robustness to noisy, conflicting, or poisoned evidence, so it should not be cited as direct evidence for unreliable-evidence robustness.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at github.com/kilgrims/ReMindRAG; fits graph_kg scenario coverage.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Systematic ablation across RAG pipeline modules (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization) identifies best-performing configurations and quantifies performance-latency trade-offs.
Fine-tuning the generator with a mix of relevant and randomly-sampled documents improves robustness to irrelevant retrieved context while preserving use of relevant evidence.
RAG workflows can be extended to multimodal settings via text2image/image2text retrieval and a retrieval-as-generation strategy for groundedness.
rationale: The paper performs a systematic search over RAG workflow choices and includes an explicit robustness experiment showing that mixing gold and random documents during generator fine-tuning yields models more robust to irrelevant context. This directly supports survey claims on evidence construction, summarization for noise reduction, and training-time strategies for unreliable evidence. It is venue-linked (EMNLP 2024) with open code and serves as a backbone reference for the evidence-construction perspective. Overclaim risk is modest since the best practices are empirically derived on specific datasets and may not generalize universally.
caveat: Best-practice claims are empirically tuned on selected QA/reasoning datasets and a specific generator (Llama2-7B), so generalization to adversarial or domain-shifted unreliable-evidence settings is not fully established.
notes: Multimodal extension is brief; main contribution is workflow-level best practices and robustness-oriented fine-tuning.

title: Semantic Retrieval Augmented Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
supports_claims: Semantic retrieval over LLM-generated embeddings can be used to construct contrastive sample pairs for sequential recommendation.
rationale: This paper proposes SRA-CL, a sequential recommendation framework that uses LLM-generated semantic embeddings to retrieve similar users/items as contrastive learning pairs. The 'retrieval augmented' terminology here refers to retrieving samples for contrastive learning in a recommender backbone, not retrieving evidence to ground LLM generation. The paper addresses none of the core RAG-under-unreliable-evidence concerns (faithfulness, knowledge conflict, hallucination, evidence sufficiency, attack/defense, abstention) and the LLM is used only offline to produce frozen embeddings for ID-based recommendation. The scenario tag 'code_math_symbolic' appears to be a mislabel; this is a recommender systems paper.
caveat: Despite the 'retrieval augmented' name and use of LLMs, the work is outside the scope of robust RAG for generation under unreliable evidence.
notes: Scenario hit appears spurious; paper is a NeurIPS 2025 sequential recommendation contrastive learning method, not a multimodal or code/math RAG system.

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: RAG can substantially reduce hallucination in structured output generation tasks such as text-to-workflow JSON, with retrieval grounding step and table names to valid lexicon entries.
A small fine-tuned dense retriever paired with a smaller LLM can match larger non-RAG models in industrial deployments while improving out-of-domain generalization.
rationale: This NAACL Industry Track paper applies RAG to structured output generation (workflow JSON), showing hallucination rates drop from up to 21% to under 7.5% for steps and 4.5% for tables when retrieved candidates are injected into the prompt. It is relevant to a robust RAG survey as a structured-output scenario case where retrieval supplies the valid lexicon and thereby constrains generation faithfulness, and it includes OOD analyses. However, it does not directly study unreliable or noisy evidence; retrieval is assumed clean and the contribution is more application-oriented, so appendix citation in a modality/scenario extension is appropriate.
caveat: Does not address adversarial, noisy, or conflicting evidence; retriever assumed near-100% recall during LLM training, limiting insight into robustness under unreliable retrieval.
notes: Industry Track paper; useful as a structured-output RAG application example.

title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
supports_claims: Self-play RL with decomposer-solver roles can improve multi-hop retrieval and reasoning without intermediate annotations.
Preference-based iterative DPO over rollouts enables adaptive query decomposition that increases passage recall and answer accuracy in complex RAG.
rationale: AceSearcher trains a single LLM to alternate as decomposer and solver via SFT plus iterative preference-based RL, targeting multi-hop QA, fact verification, and document-level reasoning. It is relevant to the survey as an action-control/adaptive-retrieval method that improves recall under reasoning-intensive retrieval, and as an agentic RAG baseline. However, it does not directly address unreliable evidence (noise, conflict, poisoning), so appendix placement under extended adaptive-retrieval coverage is appropriate rather than a main mechanistic citation.
caveat: Paper focuses on reasoning quality and decomposition, not on noise robustness, conflict resolution, or evidence reliability per se; risk of overclaiming if framed as a robustness method.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code and model artifacts publicly available.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Knowledge-graph-indexed retrieval with Personalized PageRank enables single-step multi-hop evidence aggregation, improving robustness when relevant evidence is dispersed across passages.
Neurobiologically inspired long-term memory structures provide a scalable alternative to iterative retrieval for integrating new evidence into LLMs.
rationale: HippoRAG is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that constructs an OpenIE-derived KG as a hippocampal index and uses Personalized PageRank for multi-hop retrieval, significantly outperforming standard RAG baselines on MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it represents a major venue-backbone method in the graph/KG-augmented retrieval and long-term memory lineage, directly addressing evidence construction for integrating knowledge across passages. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because the core mechanism is structurally graph-based, though it also has clear evidence_construction relevance.
caveat: Robustness to noisy or adversarial evidence is not the paper's focus; error analysis notes OpenIE/NER errors propagate, and scalability beyond benchmark-size corpora remains unvalidated.
notes: Could alternatively be placed at main:evidence; graph_kg scenario_hit aligns with agent_memory_tool framing in metadata.

title: EmbedDistill: A geometric knowledge distillation for information retrieval
supports_claims: Knowledge distillation with embedding-space alignment can produce compact dual-encoder retrievers that nearly match large teacher models on NQ and MSMARCO.
Improvements to dense retrieval backbones (e.g., asymmetric DE configurations and dual-pooled cross-encoders) underpin the retrieval stage of modern RAG systems.
rationale: EmbedDistill proposes a geometric distillation approach (embedding matching plus query generation) to compress DE and CE retrievers while preserving ranking quality on standard IR benchmarks. While it strengthens the retrieval foundation that RAG depends on, it does not address unreliable evidence, noise filtering, attribution, knowledge conflict, abstention, or any robustness/security aspect that the survey targets. It is appropriate only as a background reference for retriever-side method lineage, not as a main mechanistic citation for robust RAG.
caveat: Overclaim risk if cited as contributing to robustness; the paper is purely about distillation efficiency/quality for standard IR, not unreliable-evidence handling.
notes: Scenario tags (code_math_symbolic / long_context_doc) in metadata appear mismatched; evaluation is on NQ and MSMARCO general IR.

title: Molecule Generation with Fragment Retrieval Augmentation
supports_claims: RAG concepts can be transferred to fragment-based molecule generation by retrieving hard and soft molecular fragments to guide a pretrained molecular language model.
Fragment-level retrieval augmentation with iterative vocabulary update improves exploration-exploitation trade-offs in drug discovery benchmarks.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2024 paper adapts RAG terminology to fragment-based molecule generation, retrieving molecular fragments rather than textual evidence. It does not address unreliable evidence, knowledge conflict, faithfulness, attribution, retrieval noise, or any robustness concern central to a survey on robust RAG. The contribution is a domain-specific generative method for drug discovery, with no mechanistic insight transferable to text-based robust RAG.
caveat: Including it would risk overclaiming RAG-domain breadth without adding evidence on reliability or unreliable-evidence handling.
notes: Boundary domain application of RAG; molecular fragments are not evidence in the survey sense.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Lightweight proxy agents can mediate retriever-LLM misalignment by deciding when to retrieve, rewriting queries, and filtering retrieved documents.
Multi-agent reinforcement learning with tree-structured rollout and Monte Carlo credit assignment enables end-to-end optimization of adaptive RAG pipelines without modifying retrievers or LLMs.
rationale: C-3PO proposes a proxy-centric multi-agent framework with specialized Reasoning Router, Information Filter, and Decision Maker agents that jointly perform adaptive retrieval decisions, query generation, and document filtering, trained via MARL with Monte Carlo credit assignment. It is relevant to robust RAG because it addresses adaptive retrieval control and information filtering, which are core action-control and evidence-construction mechanisms. However, it focuses on retriever-LLM alignment and pipeline coordination rather than directly tackling unreliable, adversarial, or conflicting evidence, so it is best cited in the appendix as supporting work for adaptive routing and filtering rather than as a main backbone reference.
caveat: The paper does not explicitly evaluate robustness to noisy, poisoned, or conflicting retrieved evidence, so overclaiming its relevance to unreliable-evidence robustness should be avoided.
notes: ICML 2025 PMLR v267; code available at github.com/Chen-GX/C-3PO.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: Multi-agent reinforcement learning can jointly optimize RAG pipeline modules (query rewriter, selector, generator) toward a shared answer-quality reward, mitigating objective misalignment among components.
Including a learned document selector in the RAG pipeline helps filter noisy retrieved documents and contributes to more robust answer generation.
rationale: The paper formulates a multi-module RAG pipeline as a cooperative multi-agent RL problem and uses MAPPO with a shared F1 reward to jointly train query rewriter, selector, and generator on multi-hop QA datasets. It is relevant to robust RAG insofar as the Selector module filters noisy candidate documents and joint optimization aligns component objectives with final answer correctness, which connects to action/control aspects of robustness. However, it does not directly study unreliable-evidence settings such as poisoning, conflicting evidence, or abstention, so it is better placed as an appendix-level citation supporting the MARL/joint-optimization branch rather than a main mechanistic reference.
caveat: Robustness to unreliable or adversarial evidence is not explicitly evaluated; gains are measured on standard QA F1/EM rather than noise- or attack-stressed benchmarks.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper with public code at github.com/chenyiqun/MMOA-RAG; agentic/MARL angle for RAG control.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Iterative chain-of-retrieval with dynamic query reformulation mitigates failures of single-step retrieval on complex multi-hop queries.
Test-time scaling strategies (greedy, best-of-N, tree search) and learning-to-stop allow adaptive compute allocation based on query complexity and retriever quality.
Trained iterative retrieval pipelines remain robust across retrievers of varying strength (E5-large, E5-base, BM25).
rationale: CoRAG explicitly targets unreliable single-step retrieval by training an LLM via rejection-sampled retrieval chains to decompose queries and reformulate when retrieval fails. It provides concrete mechanisms (greedy, best-of-N, tree search, learn-to-stop) and demonstrates robustness across different retrievers and weak-to-strong generalization, all directly relevant to robust RAG under noisy evidence. Published at NeurIPS 2025 with code/data released, it is a strong main-citation backbone for the evidence-construction and action-control sections.
caveat: Focuses on short-answer QA (multi-hop QA, KILT) and does not directly address adversarial/poisoned evidence or long-form generation; robustness claims are about retriever quality, not malicious or conflicting evidence.
notes: Could alternatively be placed in main:control given the test-time scaling and learn-to-stop contributions.

title: A Neural Corpus Indexer for Document Retrieval
supports_claims: Generative retrieval methods such as NCI represent an alternative retrieval paradigm to sparse and dense retrieval underlying RAG systems.
End-to-end seq2seq document identifier generation can improve recall on standard QA benchmarks but does not address evidence reliability.
rationale: NCI is a generative retrieval method that maps queries directly to document identifiers via a seq2seq model with a prefix-aware weight-adaptive decoder, evaluated on NQ320k and TriviaQA. It is foundational to the retriever component of RAG but does not address robustness to unreliable evidence, noise, poisoning, calibration, or evidence sufficiency. Its relevance to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence is limited to background coverage of retrieval paradigms. Overclaim risk is moderate if cited as supporting robustness claims, since the paper focuses solely on recall/ranking quality.
caveat: Paper does not study reliability, faithfulness, noise robustness, or any evidence-quality issues central to the survey.
notes: NeurIPS 2022 paper; potential background citation in a retrieval paradigms subsection.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained adaptive search intensity scaling enables LLMs to escalate retrieval frequency and depth in noisy real-web environments, improving robustness over fixed prompting or SFT pipelines.
Training and evaluating iterative RAG on open-web noisy sources surfaces conflict resolution, verification/denoising, and reflection behaviors that clean Wiki benchmarks fail to elicit.
rationale: DeepDiver proposes an RL framework (GRPO over iterative RAG) that learns when and how aggressively to search, directly targeting unreliable/noisy/conflicting web evidence rather than clean Wikipedia.
