title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
supports_claims: KG-grounded RAG can improve faithfulness by distilling structural priors (relation paths) into LLMs via SFT plus preference optimization.
Reasoning-introspection with predefined constraints and backtracking can mitigate false-positive reasoning paths and improve response reliability over KGs.
rationale: The paper proposes DP, a KG-RAG framework that combines progressive knowledge distillation for faithful relation path generation with a constraint-based introspection-and-backtracking loop to verify reasoning paths before answering. This connects to robust RAG under unreliable evidence via the graph/KG modality and via an explicit action-control mechanism (verification and backtracking against extracted constraints). It is a useful case study for the modality chapter on KG-RAG and also touches the action-control theme, though its evaluation centers on standard KGQA benchmarks rather than adversarial or noisy-evidence stress tests.
caveat: Reliability gains are shown on clean KGQA datasets (WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA); robustness to noisy, conflicting, or poisoned KG evidence is not directly evaluated.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at github.com/mira-ai-lab/Deliberation-on-Priors.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
supports_claims: Unifying context ranking and answer generation via instruction tuning can filter noisy retrieved evidence and improve RAG robustness under imperfect retrieval.
Reranking with a small amount of ranking data can outperform dedicated reranker models and improve recall of relevant contexts in knowledge-intensive QA and biomedical RAG.
Selecting top-k contexts involves a recall-noise tradeoff that motivates integrated ranking within RAG pipelines.
rationale: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM to jointly rerank retrieved passages and generate answers, directly addressing the problem of noisy/irrelevant retrieved evidence that destabilizes RAG. It empirically demonstrates the tradeoff between top-k size and irrelevant context noise (Figure 1) and shows that integrated ranking improves robustness across nine general-domain and five biomedical benchmarks, including under weak retrievers. As a NeurIPS 2024 paper contributing a unified retrieve-rerank-generate pipeline, it is a strong venue-backbone citation for the evidence construction section of the survey.
caveat: Focuses on single-round retrieval and improving recall; does not directly address adversarial poisoning, abstention, or calibration under unreliable evidence.
notes: Strong evidence-construction lineage paper; useful for discussion of context filtering and recall-noise tradeoff.

title: RAGRouter: Learning to Route Queries to Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
supports_claims: LLMs differ in their ability to leverage retrieved documents and tolerate retrieval noise, motivating routing-based action control in RAG.
Score-threshold routing across heterogeneous LLMs can yield accuracy-latency trade-offs under unreliable evidence conditions including counterfactual and irrelevant noise.
rationale: The paper formulates LLM routing under RAG and proposes RAGRouter, a contrastive-learning router that models document-induced knowledge shifts and per-model RAG capability, evaluated under local, online, and noise-injected retrieval. This is relevant to a robust RAG survey as a model-selection/action-control mechanism that explicitly handles heterogeneous robustness to retrieval noise. It fits appendix or a control-section citation rather than a main backbone, since it targets routing rather than evidence construction or faithfulness directly.
caveat: Focuses on routing among LLMs rather than directly improving robustness of a single model to unreliable evidence; scenario tag table_structured in metadata is misleading.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at github.com/OwwO99/RAGRouter; noisy-retrieval subset (counterfactual/irrelevant/relevant) gives extra robustness evidence.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
supports_claims: Hallucination detection signals from internal hidden states, attention maps, and output probabilities can flag ungrounded RAG outputs efficiently in single-response settings.
RAGTruth-style span-annotated benchmarks enable evaluation of hallucination detectors under retrieval-augmented generation with both white-box and black-box access.
rationale: LLM-Check proposes lightweight single-response hallucination detection using eigenvalue analyses of attention kernels and hidden activations plus token-level uncertainty, and explicitly evaluates on RAGTruth in both white-box and black-box regimes. This is relevant to the model_evidence_use facet of robust RAG because it offers an inference-time signal for detecting ungrounded generations when references are present but possibly noisy. Appendix placement is appropriate since the contribution is general hallucination detection rather than a core RAG mechanism, and the scenario tag of table_structured in metadata does not really fit the paper's content.
caveat: Detection AUROC gains in RAG settings are modest (often 55-63), and the method does not directly model unreliable or conflicting evidence; the table_structured scenario label is not actually supported by the paper.
notes: NeurIPS 2024 venue-linked; useful as a detector baseline reference rather than a core robust-RAG method.

title: Optimizing Retrieval for RAG via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: Reinforcement learning can optimize retrievers for downstream RAG performance, addressing the gap where traditional IR retrieves semantically related but unhelpful or misleading evidence.
Environment-specific relevance signals from generation outcomes can produce better contrastive labels than static supervised fine-tuning, improving evidence quality in RAG.
rationale: The paper proposes R3, an RL framework that uses LLM generation feedback to construct on-the-fly contrastive signals for training retrievers tailored to RAG environments. It explicitly motivates the work by noting that IR retrievers often surface unhelpful, LLM-generated, or misleading evidence that degrades RAG, which is adjacent to the survey's robustness-under-unreliable-evidence theme. It fits as appendix-level coverage of evidence-construction methods that adapt retrieval via feedback rather than as a core robustness/unreliable-evidence contribution.
caveat: The paper targets generic retrieval optimization for QA-style RAG rather than directly studying poisoning, noise robustness, or unreliable-evidence handling; relevance is indirect.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper; code release promised but no URL extracted.

title: RAC: Retrieval-augmented Conversation Dataset for Open-domain Question Answering in Conversational Settings
supports_claims: Conversational RAG pipelines benefit from reranking and the quality of retrieved passages directly affects response generation quality.
Generation models can produce irrelevant responses when retrieved passages contain outdated information, suggesting weakness on temporal questions.
rationale: This is an EMNLP Industry Track paper introducing a Korean retrieval-augmented conversation (RAC) dataset and a baseline pipeline (query rewriting, BM25/dense retrieval, reranking, FiD/LLM generation). While it includes some analysis of how retrieval quality affects generation and notes failure modes on temporal questions, the core contribution is a language-specific dataset and standard system engineering, not a methodological advance for robust RAG under unreliable evidence, attribution, calibration, or adversarial settings. The findings are largely confirmatory of well-known retrieval-quality/generation correlations and do not provide distinctive evidence for the survey's robustness focus.
caveat: Citing risks overclaiming this dataset paper as a robustness contribution; its insights on retrieval quality affecting generation are standard and language/domain limited.

title: Boosting the Potential of Large Language Models with an Intelligent Information Assistant
supports_claims: Assistant/agent-based RAG architectures separate a trainable information manager from a frozen main LLM, providing planning decisions over whether retrieved memory or extracted knowledge should be used.

Two-phase training (curriculum assistant learning plus reinforced preference optimization) can align an intermediate retrieval assistant's outputs with the downstream LLM's preferences for noise-filtered evidence.
rationale: AssistRAG introduces an agentic RAG framework where a trainable assistant performs question decomposition, knowledge extraction, memory management, and explicit plan steps that assess whether retrieved memory/knowledge is useful before passing it to the main LLM. The planning components are mildly relevant to action control under unreliable evidence (gating noisy retrievals), and the architecture is representative of agent_memory_tool scenarios. Placement in the appendix/extended agent-RAG coverage fits because the paper is primarily a method/architecture contribution rather than a robustness-focused study; overclaiming its noise-robustness contributions should be avoided.
caveat: The paper does not systematically evaluate robustness to adversarial/noisy/conflicting evidence; its 'plan' steps are evaluated indirectly via QA accuracy on standard multi-hop datasets.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Token-level fusion between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence can be theoretically decomposed into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction).
The actual effect of RAG on each token can be predicted from representation similarity without training or external utility evaluators, enabling adaptive token-level use of retrieved evidence.
Training-free collaborative decoding between pure LLM and RAG improves robustness to noisy retrieved passages across QA and long-form tasks.
rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper formalizes RAG as a distribution fusion between LLM knowledge and retrieved texts, decomposing it into benefit and detriment terms tied to knowledge completion vs. contradiction, and proves these can be compared via representation similarity at token level. The proposed Tok-RAG performs collaborative pure-LLM/RAG decoding to preserve useful evidence and discard misleading content, directly addressing robustness under unreliable retrieval. It is a strong mechanistic and theoretical anchor for the survey's discussion of how LLMs should consume potentially noisy evidence, justifying a main-text citation in the model/evidence-use section. Risk: the theoretical claims rely on HMM-style latent-variable assumptions and layer-wise heuristics that may not hold for all architectures.
caveat: Theory rests on strong latent-variable/HMM assumptions and the practical method depends on heuristics for locating the 'distribution fusion' layer.
notes: Although metadata tags scenario as code_math_symbolic, the paper is a general RAG method evaluated across QA, dialogue, code, slot filling, and LM tasks.

title: Policy Learning from Tutorial Books via Understanding, Rehearsing and Introspecting
supports_claims: RAG can be repurposed to retrieve textual knowledge for generating imaginary policy-learning trajectories in agent/decision-making settings
Standard embedding-based retrieval suffers modality gaps between query states and knowledge text, motivating scope-based retrieval
rationale: This paper proposes Policy Learning from Tutorial Books (PLfB) using a three-stage URI framework that employs RAG as an auxiliary component to retrieve code-based knowledge from books and generate imaginary trajectories for offline RL. While it acknowledges LLM hallucinations and uses uncertainty-aware CQL (CIQL) to handle unreliable generated transitions/rewards, the unreliability is addressed through offline RL conservatism rather than through robust RAG mechanisms per se. The paper's core contribution is policy learning, not robust RAG under unreliable evidence, so it falls outside the survey's main scope.
caveat: The knowledge scope retrieval idea addresses a genuine RAG modality-gap problem, but the contribution is tightly coupled to policy learning and does not generalize as a robust RAG technique.
notes: Could be marginally referenced as agent/decision-making RAG application, but the survey would gain little from citing it.

title: Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Question Answering: Mutual Information Exchange and Ranking by Contrasting Layers
supports_claims: Uncertainty-masked question decomposition can reduce hallucinated retrieval queries
Layer-contrasting reranking improves separation of positives from distractors in RAG
rationale: CoopRAG proposes question unrolling with uncertainty masks, unrolling-augmented retrieval, and ranking by contrasting transformer layers for multi-hop QA. It contributes to evidence construction and partially to handling uncertain LLM knowledge, fitting a survey section on retrieval/reranking under unreliable evidence.
caveat: Method-specific framework; limited direct analysis of adversarial or noisy evidence robustness.

title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation through Drafting
supports_claims: Multi-perspective document subset sampling with parallel drafting mitigates position bias in long-context RAG
Verifier scoring over draft rationales filters unreliable drafts without instruction-tuning the generalist LM
rationale: The paper proposes a draft-then-verify RAG framework that clusters retrieved documents, generates diverse drafts with a small specialist, and verifies via a generalist LM using rationale-based confidence scoring. This directly contributes to evidence construction and reliability under noisy multi-document retrieval, with clear relevance to robust RAG.
caveat: Focused on QA accuracy and latency, not adversarial or poisoned evidence settings.

title: Attention in Large Language Models Yields Efficient Zero-Shot Re-Rankers
supports_claims: Attention-based in-context reranking offers an efficient O(1) alternative to generative LLM rerankers for evidence selection in RAG pipelines.
Calibration with content-free queries mitigates intrinsic LLM biases in attention-based relevance scoring.
rationale: The paper proposes ICR, leveraging LLM attention patterns plus calibration for efficient zero-shot reranking, evaluated on single-hop and multi-hop IR benchmarks. It relates to robust RAG via better evidence construction and reranking signals, but does not directly address unreliable evidence, conflicts, or noise robustness. Appropriate as appendix citation for reranking methodology coverage.
caveat: Focuses on reranking efficiency, not robustness to unreliable/adversarial evidence.

title: 基于汉语字词资源的检索增强生成与应用评估(Chinese Character- and Word-Based Retrieval Augmented Generation and Application)
supports_claims: RAG can augment Chinese character/word resources for language tasks
Domain-specific RAG application for Chinese linguistics
rationale: This paper applies RAG to Chinese character and word resources for language ability enhancement, focusing on linguistic resource construction rather than robustness under unreliable evidence. It does not address evidence reliability, action control, or evaluation protocols central to the survey.
caveat: Narrow application focus without robustness or unreliable-evidence contribution.
